questions.question: A can is in the shape of a cylinder such that the bottom of the can has a hemispherical raised portion which reduces the capacity of the can. If the height of the can is 34 cm and the inner diameter is 12 cm, then find the maximum capacity of juice that can be poured into the can (in cm3).
questions.question_hi: एक कैन सिलेंडर के आकार में है जिसमें कैन के नीचे एक अर्धगोलीय उभरा हुआ हिस्सा है जो कैन की क्षमता को कम करता है। यदि कैन की ऊंचाई 34 सेमी है और आंतरिक व्यास 12 सेमी है, तो कैन में डाली जा सकने वाली जूस की अधिकतम क्षमता ज्ञात करें (सेमी3 में)।
questions.solution:
Since the inner diameter of the can = 12 cm and height = 34 cm

Apparent capacity of the can = πr2h = 3.14 * 6 * 6 * 34 = 3843.36 cm3

The actual capacity of the can is less by the volume of the hemisphere at the base of the can. i.e., it is less by

2πr3/3 = 2 * 3.14 * (6)3/3 = 452.16 cm3

So, the actual capacity of the can = apparent capacity of can - volume of the hemisphere

= 3843.36 - 452.16

= 3391.2 cm3

questions.question: If n is any positive odd integer greater than 1, the n(n2 - 1) is always divisible by:
questions.question_hi: यदि n कोई भी 1 से बड़ा धनात्मक विषम पूर्णांक है, तो n(n2 - 1) हमेशा निम्नलिखित से विभाज्य होता है:
questions.solution:
n(n2-1) = n(n-1)(n+ 1) (take n=3; take least number)

=3 X 2 X 4 = 24

Always divisible by 24.

questions.question:
If the base of a right pyramid is a triangle of sides 7 cm, 24 cm, and 25 cm

and its volume is 928 cm3, then find its height.
questions.question_hi:
यदि एक समकोण पिरामिड का आधार 7 सेमी, 24 सेमी, और 25 सेमी पक्षों वाला त्रिभुज है

और इसका आयतन 928 सेमी3 है, तो इसकी ऊँचाई ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
The given base is a triangle with sides 7 cm, 24 cm, and 25 cm. Since

72 + 242 = 252, it is a right triangle with:

Base = 7 cm, Height = 24 cm, Hypotenuse = 25 cm

The area of a right triangle = 1/2 X Base X Height

= 1/2 * 7 * 24

= 84 cm2

The volume of the pyramid = 1/3 * area of base * height

928 = 1/3 X 84 X h

h = 33.14 cm

questions.question: Workers A and B alone finish a project in 24 and 36 days respectively. They start together. After 8 days, B is replaced by C who can finish the job alone in 18 days. How many more days will be needed to complete the task?
questions.question_hi: कर्मचारी A और B अकेले एक परियोजना को क्रमशः 24 और 36 दिनों में पूरा करते हैं। वे साथ में शुरू करते हैं। 8 दिनों के बाद, B की जगह C लेता है जो अकेले 18 दिनों में काम पूरा कर सकता है। कार्य पूरा करने के लिए और कितने दिन चाहिए होंगे?
questions.solution:
One day's work of A = 1/24

One day's work of B = 1/36

One day's work of A and B = (1/24) + (1/36) = 5/72

Work done by A and B in 8 days = 8 x 5/72 = 5/9 units

Remaining work = 1 - (5/9) = 4/9 units

One day's work of A and C = (1/24) + (1/18) = 7/72 units

Number of days taken by A and C = (4/9)/(7/72) = 32/7 days

questions.question: A, B, and C made certain investments and the ratio of their periods is 5:8:4 respectively. The ratio of the profits of A, B, and C is 6: 9: 5 respectively. What is the ratio of the investments of A, B, and C?

questions.question:
In a circle with centre O, AB and CD are two chords intersecting each other at point P, then which of the following is TRUE?

I: Perpendicular from centre O to chord AB divides it in two equal parts and vice versa.

II: AP * CP = BP * DP
questions.question_hi:
केंद्र O के साथ एक वृत्त में, AB और CD बिंदु P पर एक दूसरे को काटते हुए दो जीवा हैं, तो निम्नलिखित में से क्या सत्य है?

I: केंद्र O से लम्ब AB को दो समान भागों में विभाजित करता है और इसके विपरीत भी ऐसा ही।

II: AP * CP = BP * DP
questions.solution:
I:

When a perpendicular from the centre of the circle is drawn on any chord, then it divided the chord in two equal parts and vice versa is also true.

II:

If Two Chords Intersect Internally or Externally then the Product of the Lengths of the Segments are Equal.

Hence, AP * PB = CP * PD

questions.question: When 6 sweets from box A put in box B, then number of sweets in both boxes is equal. If 21 sweets from box B is transferred to box A, then number of sweets in box A becomes thrice the number of sweets in box B. Find the ratio of number of sweets in box A to that of box B.
questions.question_hi: जब बॉक्स A से 6 मिठाइयाँ बॉक्स B में डाली जाती हैं, तो दोनों बॉक्सों में मिठाइयों की संख्या समान हो जाती है। यदि बॉक्स B से 21 मिठाइयाँ बॉक्स A में स्थानांतरित की जाती हैं, तो बॉक्स A में मिठाइयों की संख्या बॉक्स B की मिठाइयों की संख्या का तीन गुना हो जाती है। बॉक्स A में मिठाइयों की संख्या और बॉक्स B में मिठाइयों की संख्या का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Let the number of sweets in box B = m

The number of sweets in box A = m + 6 + 6 = m + 12

(m + 12) + 21 = 3(m - 21)

m + 33 = 3m - 63

2m = 96

m = 48

So, the ratio of number of sweets in box A to that of box B = (48 + 12):48 = 60:48 = 5:4

questions.question: A fair die is thrown. Given that the outcome is a proper divisor of 12, find the probability that it is prime.
questions.question_hi: एक निष्पक्ष पासा फेंका गया है। दिया गया है कि परिणाम 12 का एक उचित भाजक है, तो इसके अभाज्य होने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Let A = "outcome is prime"

Let B = "outcome is a proper divisor of 12"

Conditional probability formula:

P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)

Proper divisors of 12 = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}

So, |B| = 5

P(B) = 5/6

Prime numbers within {1, 2, 3, 4, 6} = {2, 3}

So, |A ∩ B| = 2

P(A ∩ B) = 2/6

P(A | B) = (2/6) ÷ (5/6) = 2/5

questions.question: In a bag, there are cups of three sizes (S1, S2, and S3) in the ratio of 6: 11: 7. If number of cups of size S2 is 24 less than the sum of number of cups of size S1 and S3, then how many total cups are there in the bag?
questions.question_hi: एक बैग में, तीन आकारों (S1, S2, और S3) के कप 6: 11: 7 के अनुपात में हैं। यदि S2 आकार के कपों की संख्या S1 और S3 आकार के कपों की संख्या के योग से 24 कम है, तो बैग में कुल कितने कप हैं?
questions.solution:
Let number of cups of sizes S1, S2, and S3 are 6x, 11x and 7x respectively.

According to the question,

11x = (6x + 7x) - 24

=> 13x - 11x = 24

=> 2x = 24

=> x = 12

So, total number of cups = 24 * 12 = 288

questions.question:
Let P = {5,6,7,5,8,9,5,6,7,8,5,10,6,8} and Q = {6,7,5,6,6,8,9,6,7,8,6,7,9,6}. Which statement(s) is/are true?

(I) Mode of P = Mode of Q − 1

(II) Mode of P + 2 = Mode of Q

options.label: D
options.text_hi: न तो I और न ही II

questions.solution:
In P, frequencies: 5→4, 6→3, 7→2, 8→3, Mode(P)=5

In Q, frequencies: 6→6, 7→3, 8→2, Mode(Q)=6

Mode(Q)−1 = 6−1 = 5 = Mode(P) => I true

Mode(P)+ 2 = 5+2 = 7 => II False

questions.question: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle. If the lateral surface area of prism and the volume of the prism is 1440 cm2 and 2880√3 cm3 respectively, then find the side of the base of the prism.
questions.question_hi: एक समकोण प्रिज्म का आधार एक समबाहु त्रिभुज है। यदि प्रिज्म का पार्श्व सतह क्षेत्रफल और प्रिज्म का आयतन क्रमशः 1440 सेमी2 और 2880√3 सेमी3 है, तो प्रिज्म के आधार का पक्ष ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Let the base of prism and height of the prism be 'a' cm and h cm respectively.

Lateral surface area of the prism = Perimeter of base * height

3 * a * h = 1440

ah = 480

The volume of the prism = Area of base * height

√3/4 * a2 * h = 2880√3

a * 480 = 2880 * 4

a = 24 cm

questions.question: Non-parallel sides of a trapezium are of same length which are of length 10 cm and the distance between the parallel sides of the trapezium is 6 cm. If smaller parallel side of the trapezium is 4 cm, then what is the product of the diagonals of the trapezium (in cm2)?
questions.question_hi: एक ट्रैपेजियम के गैर-समानांतर पक्ष समान लंबाई के हैं जो 10 सेमी हैं और ट्रैपेजियम के समानांतर पक्षों के बीच की दूरी 6 सेमी है। यदि ट्रैपेजियम का छोटा समानांतर पक्ष 4 सेमी है, तो ट्रैपेजियम के विकर्णों का गुणनफल (सेमी2 में) क्या होगा?
questions.solution:
Given, AD = BC = 10 cm

CD = EF = 4 cm and DE = CF = 6 cm

In ∆BCF,

BC2 = BF2 + CF2

=> 102 = BF2 + 62

=> BF2 = 100 - 36

=> BF2 = 64

=> BF = 8 cm

Similarly, AE = 8 cm

So, AF = 8 + 4 = 12 cm

In ∆ACF,

AC2 = AF2 + CF2

=> AC2 = 122 + 62 = 180

=> AC = √180 = 6√5 cm

Similarly, BD = 6√5 cm

Therefore, product of the diagonals of the trapezium = AC * BD = 6√5 * 6√5 = 180 cm2

questions.question: A cuboidal tank has internal dimensions 20 cm long, 16 cm wide, and 9 cm high. If a solid sphere of the maximum possible radius is placed inside this tank, what is the volume of the unoccupied space in the tank?
questions.question_hi: एक घनाभाकार टैंक के आंतरिक आयाम 20 सेमी लंबाई, 16 सेमी चौड़ाई और 9 सेमी ऊँचाई हैं। यदि इस टैंक के अंदर अधिकतम संभव त्रिज्या का एक ठोस गोला रखा जाता है, तो टैंक में खाली स्थान का आयतन क्या होगा?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid = 20*16*9 = 2880 cm3

Maximum possible radius of sphere = 9/2 cm

Volume of sphere = 4/3 * 22/7 * (9/2)3 = 381.86 cm3

Volume of the unoccupied space = 2880 - 381.86 = 2498.14 cm3

questions.question: ΔMNO is right angled at N and P is any point on the side ON. If OM = 26 cm, PM = 25 cm, and OP = 3 cm, then find the length of side MN.

questions.solution:
OM = 26 cm

PM = 25 cm

OP = 3 cm

In ΔMNP,

PM2 = MN2 + PN2

252 = MN2 + PN2 ......... (1)

In ΔMNO,

OM2 = MN2 + ON2

262 = MN2 + (OP + PN)2

262 = MN2 + (3 + PN)2

262 = MN2 + 9 + PN2 + 6PN ...... (2)

From (1) and (2):

9 + 6PN = 262 - 252

6PN = 42

PN = 7

From equation (1):

625 = MN2 + 72

MN = 24 cm

A right circular cone is inscribed in a cube of side 42 cm such that its base lies on one face and its vertex touches the opposite face. Using π = 22/7, find the volume of the largest such cone (in cm3).
questions.question_hi: एक समकोणीय वृत्तीय शंकु को 42 सेमी के पक्ष वाले घन में इस प्रकार अंकित किया गया है कि इसका आधार एक चेहरे पर स्थित है और इसका शीर्ष विपरीत चेहरे को छूता है। π = 22/7 का उपयोग करते हुए, सबसे बड़े ऐसे शंकु का आयतन (सेमी3 में) ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Largest cone in this setting has radius r = s/2 and height h = s, where s = cube side.

volume of cone (V) = 1/3 πr2h

Given:

s = 42

=> r = 42/2 = 21, h = 42

V = (1/3) X (22/7) X (212) X 42

212 = 441

(1/3) X 42 = 14

V = (22/7) X 441 X 14

441 ÷ 7 = 63

V = 22 X 63 X 14

V = 22 X 882

=> 19404

In the following question, two statements are given and two conclusions are given below these statements. Choose the option which shows the conclusions which logically follow from the given statements, disregarding the commonly known facts.

Only a few Teacher is Scholar

No Scholar is Academic

Conclusions:

I. Some Scholar is Academic

II. All Teacher cannot be Academic
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में, दो कथन दिए गए हैं और इन कथनों के नीचे दो निष्कर्ष दिए गए हैं। उस विकल्प को चुनें जो दिए गए कथनों से तार्किक रूप से निकले निष्कर्षों को दर्शाता है, सामान्यतः ज्ञात तथ्यों की परवाह किए बिना।

कथन:

केवल कुछ शिक्षक विद्वान हैं

कोई विद्वान अकादमिक नहीं है

निष्कर्ष:

I. कुछ विद्वान अकादमिक हैं

II. सभी शिक्षक अकादमिक नहीं हो सकते

options.label: A
options.text_hi: केवल निष्कर्ष I अनुसरण करता है

options.label: B
options.text_hi: केवल निष्कर्ष II अनुसरण करता है

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.text_hi: दोनों निष्कर्ष I और II अनुसरण करते हैं

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.text_hi: न तो निष्कर्ष I और न ही II अनुसरण करता है

questions.solution:
Statements:

Only a few Teacher is Scholar

No Scholar is Academic

Some Scholar is Academic: No Scholar is Academic. So, conclusion I is false.

All Teacher cannot be Academic: Only a few Teacher is Scholar means some Teacher is Scholar and some Teacher is not Scholar. Thus, the Teacher which is Scholar cannot be Academic. So, conclusion II is true.

Hence, only conclusion II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'mint tea' is written as 'ka lo', 'tea lemon' is written as 'lo su' and 'mint honey basil' is written as 'ta vi ka'. Each word is coded by a distinct code. Which of the following codes can represent 'honey'?
questions.question_hi: एक निश्चित कोड भाषा में, 'mint tea' को 'ka lo' के रूप में लिखा जाता है, 'tea lemon' को 'lo su' के रूप में लिखा जाता है और 'mint honey basil' को 'ta vi ka' के रूप में लिखा जाता है। प्रत्येक शब्द को एक अलग कोड द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कोड 'honey' का प्रतिनिधित्व कर सकता है?
questions.solution:
From 'mint tea' = 'ka lo' and 'tea lemon' = 'lo su', the common word is 'tea' and the common code is 'lo', so tea = lo.

Then in 'mint tea' = 'ka lo', the remaining code gives mint = ka

Now 'mint honey basil' = 'ta vi ka'. Since mint = ka, remove 'ka' from this statement.

So the remaining codes 'ta' and 'vi' are for 'honey' and 'basil' in some order.

Therefore, 'honey' can be coded as 'ta' or 'vi'.

Among the options, only 'vi' matches a possible code for 'honey'.

Answer: vi

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The librarian maintains detailed records of all issued reference books in the central register.

options.label: A
options.text: Detailed records of all issued reference books were maintained in the central register by the librarian.

options.label: B
options.text: Detailed records of all issued reference books are maintained in the central register by the librarian.

options.label: C
options.text: Detailed records of all issued reference books have been maintained in the central register by the librarian.

options.label: D
options.text: The librarian is maintained detailed records of all issued reference books in the central register.

questions.correct_text: Detailed records of all issued reference books are maintained in the central register by the librarian.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ["are" in this case] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in the present indefinite, as indicated by the verb "maintains". Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the present indefinite.

The format of the Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Active: She teaches English.

Passive: English is taught by her.

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the tone of the passage?
questions.solution: The passage thoughtfully examines differing perspectives on progress, weighing linear and cyclical models and considering their implications without appealing to emotion or telling a story. This reflective and analytical approach defines its tone. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

The concept of progress has long been central to human thought, yet its nature remains deeply contested. While some view progress as a linear movement towards continuous improvement, others argue that it is cyclical, marked by recurring patterns of rise and decline. The debate between linear and cyclical models of progress reflects broader philosophical questions about history, development, and human agency. The linear view of progress suggests that humanity advances steadily over time through scientific discovery, technological innovation, and social reform. This perspective is rooted in Enlightenment thinking, which promoted the belief that reason and knowledge could overcome ignorance, superstition, and suffering. From this standpoint, each generation builds upon the achievements of the previous one, leading to higher standards of living, greater political freedoms, and expanded opportunities. Developments in medicine, education, and communication often serve as evidence of this forward trajectory.

In contrast, the cyclical view of progress challenges the assumption of permanent advancement. According to this perspective, history moves in repetitive cycles of growth, stagnation, and decline. Ancient civilisations such as those of Rome, Greece, and Egypt reached remarkable heights, only to collapse due to internal decay or external pressures. Cyclical theorists argue that modern societies are not exempt from similar patterns, as technological progress is frequently accompanied by moral, ecological, or political crises. War, environmental degradation, and social inequality suggest that human problems persist despite material advancement. Furthermore, the cyclical model emphasises that progress in one domain may coincide with regression in another. While digital technology has improved access to information, it has also intensified surveillance, reduced privacy, and contributed to social isolation. This indicates that progress is neither uniform nor irreversible but shaped by complex trade-offs.

A more balanced understanding may lie in recognising progress as both linear and cyclical. Certain advancements, such as literacy or life expectancy, show long-term improvement, yet societies also experience recurring conflicts and challenges. Progress, therefore, is not a simple upward line but a dynamic process influenced by human choices and historical conditions. Thus, the debate between linear and cyclical progress reveals that development is neither guaranteed nor meaningless. While humanity demonstrates a capacity for innovation and growth, it also repeats patterns of error and crisis. True progress depends not merely on technological change but on ethical reflection and responsible action.

questions.question: The word "irreversible" as used in the passage most nearly means:
questions.solution: The passage states that progress "is neither uniform nor irreversible," implying that progress is not permanent or unchangeable. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

You are advised to complete the online registration process well before the deadline.

options.label: A
options.text: You should be completed the online registration process well before the deadline.

options.label: B
options.text: Complete the online registration process well before the deadline.

options.label: C
options.text: Please completing the online registration process well before the deadline.

options.label: D
options.text: You will complete the online registration process well before the deadline.

questions.correct_text: Complete the online registration process well before the deadline.
questions.solution:
The Passive Voice construction "You are advised to" is removed to form an imperative Active Voice sentence.

Imperative sentences begin with the base form of the verb and are commonly used for advice, requests, or instructions.

The sentence in the active voice is in imperative form. An imperative sentence is used to express an order, request, or suggestion.

Passive voice format: You are advised to + V1 + Object.

Active voice format: V1 + Object.

For example:

Passive: You are advised to follow the instructions carefully.

Active: Follow the instructions carefully.

Only option (b) follows all the conditions correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question: Which of the following can fit in the blank A?
questions.solution:
The blank needs a verb that fits the context of introducing or presenting "significant challenges".

The verb poses means to present or constitute a problem, danger, or difficulty. The phrase "poses a challenge" is a standard and appropriate collocation.

Option a) Submits - It means to yield or surrender to a superior force, which is contextually incorrect. The gig economy doesn't submit to challenges; it creates them.

Option b) Invokes - It means to cite or appeal to someone or something as an authority for an action, which does not fit the context of creating challenges.

Option c) Conceals - It means to hide. The gig economy's challenges are being discussed, not hidden, so this is the opposite of the intended meaning.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The gig economy, characterized by short-term contracts and freelance work, is reshaping traditional employment models. While it offers flexibility and autonomy, it also (A) ______ significant challenges regarding worker rights and job security. Many gig workers are classified as independent contractors, a status that often (B) ______ them of benefits like health insurance and paid leave. This classification is a point of intense legal and ethical (C) ______ globally. Advocates argue for a new framework that balances the innovative nature of these platforms with the need for fair labour protections. (D) ______, creating a sustainable future for the gig economy depends on addressing these disparities. Such reforms are (E) ______ to ensure that technological progress does not come at the cost of human dignity.

questions.question: Which of the following can fit in the blank B?
questions.solution:
The blank requires a verb that describes the effect of the "independent contractor" status on workers' access to benefits. The context is negative, suggesting a loss.

The verb deprives means to deny a person or place the possession or use of something. The phrase "deprives them of benefits" perfectly captures the idea that this status prevents workers from receiving benefits.

Option a) Grants - It means to give or allow, which is the exact opposite of the intended meaning.

Option c) Assures - It means to promise or tell someone something positively to dispel any doubts. The status does not assure them of benefits; it takes them away.

Option d) Equips - It means to supply with necessary items for a particular purpose, which is contextually inappropriate.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Rahul drew the curtain in the morning.

options.label: A
options.text: The curtain was drawn by Rahul in the morning.

options.label: B
options.text: The curtain had been drawn by Rahul in the morning.

options.label: C
options.text: The curtain was been drawn by Rahul in the morning.

options.label: D
options.text: The curtain is drew by Rahul in the morning.

questions.correct_text: The curtain was drawn by Rahul in the morning.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a helping verb [was] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Subject (Objective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Object (Subjective Case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a) The curtain was drawn by Rahul in the morning.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The guide assured the tourists that they would be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak the following morning if the weather permitted.

options.label: A
options.text: The guide said to the tourists, "You could be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak tomorrow morning if the weather permits."

options.label: B
options.text: The guide said to the tourists, "You will be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak tomorrow morning if the weather permits."

options.label: C
options.text: The guide said to the tourists, "We will be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak the next morning if the weather permits."

options.label: D
options.text: The guide said to the tourists, "They shall be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak tomorrow morning if the weather permitted."

questions.correct_text: The guide said to the tourists, "You will be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak tomorrow morning if the weather permits."
questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Conditional Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Continuous Tense.

Conditional Continuous (Subject + would/should + be + V1 +ing) will be converted into Future Continuous (Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing).

For example:

He said that he would be using the book next Friday. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I will be using the book next Friday" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'assured the tourists that' is changed to 'said to the tourists,'.

'they' is changed to 'You'.

'would be witnessing' is changed to 'will be witnessing'.

'the following morning' is changed to 'tomorrow morning'.

Also, inverted commas ("...") are placed in direct speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The guide said to the tourists, "You will be witnessing a spectacular sunrise from the mountain peak tomorrow morning if the weather permits."

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, what role did ornamentation play for men in ancient societies?

options.label: A
options.text: It symbolised authority, status, and cultural identity.

options.label: B
options.text: It represented emotional sensitivity and personal preference.

options.label: C
options.text: It functioned mainly as religious or spiritual symbolism.

options.label: D
options.text: It indicated rebellion against established social norms.

questions.correct_text: It symbolised authority, status, and cultural identity.
questions.solution: The passage states: "Historically, men across ancient and pre-modern societies embraced ornamentation openly and confidently, using it as a marker of power, status, identity, and cultural pride rather than as an indicator of gender expression or personal identity." (Paragraph 1) This line clearly establishes ornamentation as a symbol of authority, social position, and identity rather than personal or emotional expression. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In contemporary society, the use of ornaments, particularly bold or expressive statement pieces by men, is often linked to non-traditional expressions of masculinity. Jewellery, decorative accessories, and elaborate styling are frequently viewed as deviations from conventional male norms. However, this perception is largely a modern construct. Historically, men across ancient and pre-modern societies embraced ornamentation openly and confidently, using it as a marker of power, status, identity, and cultural pride rather than as an indicator of gender expression or personal identity. In earlier periods, adornment was an integral part of male self-presentation. Men wore heavy necklaces, armlets, rings, earrings, crowns, and richly embellished garments. These were not subtle additions but commanding visual statements meant to convey authority, courage, and social standing. Ornamentation functioned as a symbolic language, communicating hierarchy, lineage, achievement, and wealth. Far from diminishing masculinity, such embellishment reinforced it by projecting dominance and legitimacy. Across cultures, male ornamentation was normalised and respected. Warriors decorated their armour and bodies to inspire fear and admiration. Rulers used precious metals and gemstones to assert sovereignty. Even beyond elite classes, men used ornaments to signify profession, community affiliation, or life milestones. Strength, beauty, and decoration were not treated as opposing qualities; instead, they coexisted naturally within cultural norms.

The gradual decline of male ornamentation began with the rise of industrialisation and modern notions of masculinity, particularly influenced by Western ideals. Efficiency, restraint, uniformity, and practicality became dominant values. Decorative expression was increasingly seen as unnecessary or excessive, and emotional or aesthetic display in men was discouraged. Over time, ornamentation became gendered, and expressive adornment by men was viewed as unconventional. In this restrictive framework, certain communities became more willing to reclaim ornamentation as a form of visibility, individuality, and resistance to rigid norms. Jewellery and bold accessories emerged as tools to challenge narrow definitions of masculinity and assert personal freedom. As a result, ornamentation gradually became associated with alternative identities, not because it inherently belonged to them, but because they resisted imposed limitations more openly. This modern association obscures historical reality. Ornaments have never been exclusive to any one gender or identity. Their meanings are socially constructed and constantly evolving. Revisiting the past reminds us that male adornment was once a symbol of strength, not deviation. Recognising this shift allows for a more inclusive understanding of masculinity, one that acknowledges expression, aesthetics, and identity as fluid cultural practices rather than fixed categories.

options.text: Traders wearing ornaments to display commercial success

options.label: C
options.text: Artists using jewellery to express individual creativity

questions.solution: The passage states: "Warriors decorated their armour and bodies to inspire fear and admiration." (Paragraph 1) This example directly illustrates how ornamentation was respected and functional within cultural norms, especially in reinforcing masculinity and authority. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In contemporary society, the use of ornaments, particularly bold or expressive statement pieces by men, is often linked to non-traditional expressions of masculinity. Jewellery, decorative accessories, and elaborate styling are frequently viewed as deviations from conventional male norms. However, this perception is largely a modern construct. Historically, men across ancient and pre-modern societies embraced ornamentation openly and confidently, using it as a marker of power, status, identity, and cultural pride rather than as an indicator of gender expression or personal identity. In earlier periods, adornment was an integral part of male self-presentation. Men wore heavy necklaces, armlets, rings, earrings, crowns, and richly embellished garments. These were not subtle additions but commanding visual statements meant to convey authority, courage, and social standing. Ornamentation functioned as a symbolic language, communicating hierarchy, lineage, achievement, and wealth. Far from diminishing masculinity, such embellishment reinforced it by projecting dominance and legitimacy. Across cultures, male ornamentation was normalised and respected. Warriors decorated their armour and bodies to inspire fear and admiration. Rulers used precious metals and gemstones to assert sovereignty. Even beyond elite classes, men used ornaments to signify profession, community affiliation, or life milestones. Strength, beauty, and decoration were not treated as opposing qualities; instead, they coexisted naturally within cultural norms.

The gradual decline of male ornamentation began with the rise of industrialisation and modern notions of masculinity, particularly influenced by Western ideals. Efficiency, restraint, uniformity, and practicality became dominant values. Decorative expression was increasingly seen as unnecessary or excessive, and emotional or aesthetic display in men was discouraged. Over time, ornamentation became gendered, and expressive adornment by men was viewed as unconventional. In this restrictive framework, certain communities became more willing to reclaim ornamentation as a form of visibility, individuality, and resistance to rigid norms. Jewellery and bold accessories emerged as tools to challenge narrow definitions of masculinity and assert personal freedom. As a result, ornamentation gradually became associated with alternative identities, not because it inherently belonged to them, but because they resisted imposed limitations more openly. This modern association obscures historical reality. Ornaments have never been exclusive to any one gender or identity. Their meanings are socially constructed and constantly evolving. Revisiting the past reminds us that male adornment was once a symbol of strength, not deviation. Recognising this shift allows for a more inclusive understanding of masculinity, one that acknowledges expression, aesthetics, and identity as fluid cultural practices rather than fixed categories.

questions.question: What development does the passage identify as contributing to the decline of male ornamentation?

options.label: A
options.text: The spread of democratic and egalitarian values.

options.label: B
options.text: The increasing scarcity of precious decorative materials.

options.label: C
options.text: The decline of hereditary power and ruling classes.

options.label: D
options.text: The rise of industrialisation and modern masculine ideals.

questions.correct_text: The rise of industrialisation and modern masculine ideals.
questions.solution: The passage states: "The gradual decline of male ornamentation began with the rise of industrialisation and modern notions of masculinity." (Paragraph 2) The passage explicitly links industrialisation and changing masculine ideals to reduced acceptance of male ornamentation. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: What is the grammatical role of the phrase "across ancient and pre-modern societies" in the sentence, "Historically, men across ancient and pre-modern societies embraced ornamentation openly and confidently, using it as a marker of power, status, identity, and cultural pride rather than as an indicator of gender expression or personal identity"?
questions.solution:
The phrase "across ancient and pre-modern societies" modifies the verb "embraced" by indicating the scope or extent of the action, thereby functioning as an adverbial phrase.

Adjective phrase: An adjective phrase would need to modify the noun "men" directly to describe a quality (e.g., "men who were wealthy"). While it follows the noun, its primary job here is to set the geographic and temporal scope for the verb "embraced."

Noun phrase: A noun phrase acts as a subject or object (e.g., "The ancient societies"). This phrase cannot stand alone as a noun because it is headed by the preposition "across."

Prepositional subject: In English grammar, a "subject" is almost always a noun or pronoun. While a prepositional phrase can occasionally act as a subject (e.g., "Under the bridge is a shortcut"), it is not the case here; "men" is the clear subject of the sentence.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

“It is informed that the preliminary notifications for land acquisition for the highway have already been issued,” the MHA official said.

options.label: A
options.text: The MHA official said that it is informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway had already been issued.

options.label: B
options.text: The MHA official said that it was informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway have already been issued.

options.label: C
options.text: The MHA official said that it had been informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway had already been issued.

options.label: D
options.text: The MHA official said that it was informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway had already been issued.

questions.correct_text: The MHA official said that it was informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway had already been issued.
questions.solution:
The present indefinite tense ["is informed] changes into past indefinite ["was informed"] and present perfect ["have already been issued] changes into past perfect tense ["had already been issued"].

"That" should be used to join both clauses."

So, the correct sentence will be: The MHA official said that it was informed that the preliminary notification for land acquisition for the highway had already been issued.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The revised circular regarding examination norms was issued by the university authorities last week.

options.label: A
options.text: The university authorities issued the revised circular regarding examination norms last week.

options.label: B
options.text: The revised circular regarding examination norms issued the university authorities last week.

options.label: C
options.text: The university authorities are issuing the revised circular regarding examination norms last week.

options.label: D
options.text: The revised circular regarding examination norms has been issued by the university authorities last week.

questions.correct_text: The university authorities issued the revised circular regarding examination norms last week.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice ("the revised circular regarding examination norms") is changed into the object of the Active Voice, and the object ("the university authorities") becomes the subject.

The removal of the "to be" verb ["was" in this case] and the preposition "by" is necessary.

The Passive Voice is in the Simple Past tense. Hence, the Active Voice must also be in the Simple Past tense.

Passive voice format: Object + was + V3 + by + Subject

Active voice format: Subject + V2 + Object

For example:

Passive: The notice was released by the office.

Active: The office released the notice.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

My grandmother often tells us, "A little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, goes a long way in making the world a better place for everyone."

options.label: A
options.text: My grandmother often told us that a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, went a long way in making the world a better place for everyone.

options.label: B
options.text: My grandmother often tells us that a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, had gone a long way in making the world a better place for everyone.

options.label: C
options.text: My grandmother often tells us if a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, goes a long way in making the world a better place for everyone.

options.label: D
options.text: My grandmother often tells us that a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, goes a long way in making the world a better place for everyone.

questions.correct_text: My grandmother often tells us that a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, goes a long way in making the world a better place for everyone.
questions.solution:
When the reporting verb in Direct Speech is in the Present Tense (e.g., 'says', 'tells'), there is no change in the tense of the reported speech. The statement being a habitual truth also supports keeping the tense unchanged.

For Example:

Arnab says, "I want to be the best English teacher in India." (Direct Speech)

Arnab says that he wants to be the best English teacher in India. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

The conjunction "that" is added.

The reporting verb "tells" is in the present tense, so the tense of the reported speech ("goes") will not change.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "My grandmother often tells us that a little act of kindness, like sharing a meal, goes a long way in making the world a better place for everyone."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The legal advisory panel will have finalized the contractual terms after extensive consultations with all stakeholders.

options.label: A
options.text: The contractual terms are finalized after extensive consultations with all stakeholders by the legal advisory panel.

options.label: B
options.text: The contractual terms will be finalized after extensive consultations with all stakeholders by the legal advisory panel.

options.label: C
options.text: The contractual terms will have been finalized after extensive consultations with all stakeholders by the legal advisory panel.

options.label: D
options.text: The legal advisory panel will have been finalized by the contractual terms after extensive consultations with all stakeholders.

questions.correct_text: The contractual terms will have been finalized after extensive consultations with all stakeholders by the legal advisory panel.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ["been" in this case] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Perfect, shown by the structure "will have finalized." Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Future Perfect.

The format of Active Voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive Voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

The helping verb to be added is ["been" in this case].

For example:

Active: She will have completed the task.

Passive: The task will have been completed by her.

Option (c) correctly follows this structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (c).

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division are basic mathematical operations.

B. And finally division is dividing one number by another and finding the quotient and remainder.

C. The third operation, multiplication is multiplying one number with another number.

D. First operation, addition is adding of given numbers and subtraction is finding their difference.
questions.solution:
The given sentences are about basic mathematical operations. A lays the foundation of what the sentences are about. So, it will be the first sentence in the sequence. D begins with 'first operation' signifying 'addition' and so it will be the second sentence. While looking at the other two sentences, they explain the other two operations. A key word to note is 'finally' [at last] in sentence B, which makes it the last sentence of the sequence. Therefore, the final sequence of the sentences is ADCB.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It prioritises being "right" over maintaining harmony, resulting in unnecessary arguments and tension.

B. A strong ego fosters self-centeredness, making it difficult to empathise with or acknowledge the other person's feelings and perspectives.

C. It often prevents individuals from apologising or admitting mistakes, leading to unresolved conflicts and resentment.

D. Ego can destroy relationships by creating barriers to trust, communication, and emotional intimacy.
questions.solution:
After analysing the sentences, we can form the following pairs:

D and C: Sentence D introduces the idea that the ego can destroy relationships by creating barriers to trust, communication, and emotional intimacy. Sentence C follows logically, explaining that the ego often prevents individuals from apologising or admitting mistakes, which leads to unresolved conflicts and resentment.

B and A: Sentence B elaborates on how a strong ego fosters self-centeredness, making it difficult to empathise with or acknowledge the other person's feelings. Sentence A follows, showing that this ego-driven mindset prioritises being "right" over maintaining harmony, resulting in unnecessary arguments and tension.

The correct order of sentences is DCBA. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Live on a borrowed line

options.label: B
options.text: Take undue credit for others' work

questions.solution:
Live on a borrowed line: To live in a precarious or uncertain situation, relying on borrowed resources or time.

Among the given options, 'depend on borrowed time' is the correct meaning of the given idiom.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate pronoun to fill in the blank.

The board of directors gave ________ full support to the new CEO's ambitious plan for international market expansion.
questions.solution:
The sentence describes the action of "The board of directors," which is giving support. The blank requires a possessive determiner/adjective to modify "full support." The key is to determine whether a collective noun like "board" should be treated as singular or plural.

The correct option is "its". In both British and American English, a collective noun like "board," "committee," "team," or "government" is often treated as a single, singular entity when it is acting in unison as one body. Since the board is giving its unified support, treating it as a singular entity ("it") is appropriate, and the corresponding possessive is "its."

The other options are incorrect: "them" is an objective pronoun; "their" could be used (especially in British English) if the focus was on the individual members of the board, but "its" is more common when the group acts as a single unit; "themselves" is a reflexive pronoun.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "The board of directors gave its full support to the new CEO's ambitious plan for international market expansion."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note:

Collective Noun: It is the name given to a number (or collection) of persons or things taken together and spoken of as one whole. Examples could be crowd, fleet, committee, family, army, jury, heard, etc. When a collective noun acts as a single unit, it is treated as singular. When the individual members of the group are emphasized, it can be treated as plural.

Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

Reflexive Pronouns: Reflexive pronouns include myself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, and themselves. These are used to refer back to the subject of the clause in which they are used: She hurt herself in the eye.

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The customer service representative had to _____ a difficult client who was unhappy with the service.
questions.solution:
The given sentence is about the customer service representative having to do something with a difficult client who was unhappy with the service. Among the given options, 'deal with' fits because it means to handle or manage a situation, aligning with the idea of managing a difficult client. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: The customer service representative had to deal with a difficult client who was unhappy with the service.

Put off: To postpone or delay something.

Put out: To extinguish something or to cause inconvenience.

Run out of: To exhaust the supply of something.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The mountaineers faced __________ challenges while ascending the treacherous peak.
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given options.

Superficial: slight; not much.

Trivial: having little value or importance.

Unimportant: not important.

Formidable: causing you to have fear or respect for something or someone because that thing or person is large, powerful, or difficult.

"Formidable" is the correct answer as it means extremely difficult, challenging, or intimidating, which would be suitable for the challenges faced while ascending a treacherous peak. The other options do not represent the same level of difficulty.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The mountaineers faced formidable challenges while ascending the treacherous peak.

questions.question:
Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence.

If I (was) you right now, I would reconsider that risky financial investment decision.
questions.solution:
The bracketed word "was" is used in a conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact situation (the speaker is not actually "you"). In such Type 2 conditional sentences (if + simple past, ...would + base verb), the subjunctive mood "were" is traditionally used for all persons with the verb "to be" in the "if" clause, instead of "was" for "I/he/she/it." Therefore, "was" is considered grammatically incorrect in formal contexts.

Option (b) "were" is the correct subjunctive form to use in this hypothetical conditional sentence.

The correct sentence is: "If I were you right now, I would reconsider that risky financial investment decision."

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Option a): "am" is present indicative and incorrect for a hypothetical condition.

Option c): "had been" would form a Type 3 conditional (past hypothetical), which doesn't fit "right now" or the "would + base verb" structure in the main clause.

Option d): "being" is a participle and cannot function as the main verb in the "if" clause here.

Note:

· Subjunctive Mood: The subjunctive mood is used to express wishes, proposals, suggestions, or to state hypothetical or unreal conditions. In "if" clauses expressing unreal conditions, "were" is used for all subjects with the verb "to be."

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Walking down the corridor, the painting caught Anna's eye.

options.label: A
options.text: the painting was saw by Anna

options.label: B
options.text: Anna was caught by the painting's eye

questions.solution:
The grammar concept of "dangling modifier and logical subject-verb agreement" applies here. In sentences beginning with a participial phrase such as "Walking down the corridor," the main clause must have a sentient subject capable of performing the action described in the participle.

The highlighted part is wrong because "the painting" cannot perform the action of noticing; this creates a dangling modifier. The sentient subject (Anna) must be performing the action.

Option (a) - incorrect

Ungrammatical; "was saw" is incorrect; proper passive would be "was seen."

Option (b) - incorrect

Semantically illogical; implies the painting has agency to "catch" Anna's attention actively.

Option (c) - correct

Anna, the sentient subject, now performs the action of "noticed"; the sentence is grammatically and semantically coherent.

Option (d) - incorrect

Ungrammatical; a painting cannot "notice" anything.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

Note: Participial phrases must logically modify the subject of the main clause to avoid dangling modifiers. The subject must be capable of performing the action in the participle.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of the interjection.

"Alas!" he said / cheerfully, "our project / received the / highest funding."
questions.solution:
"Alas!" is an interjection used to express sorrow, regret, or disappointment. In this sentence, the speaker is cheerful and announcing that their project received the highest funding, which is a positive outcome.

Therefore, using "Alas!" is contextually inappropriate.

A more suitable interjection would be: "Hurray!"

So, there is an error in the part in option a).

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

The correct sentence is: "Hurray!" he said cheerfully, "our project received the highest funding."

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

After I accidentally washed my favourite wool sweater in hot water, (1)/ I was dismayed to see that it had shrank significantly, (2)/ becoming so small that it would now only fit (3)/ a young child instead of a grown adult. (4)

options.label: A
options.text: a young child instead of a grown adult (4)

options.label: B
options.text: After I accidentally washed my favourite wool sweater in hot water, (1)

options.label: C
options.text: becoming so small that it would now only fit (3)

options.label: D
options.text: I was dismayed to see that it had shrank significantly, (2)

questions.correct_text: I was dismayed to see that it had shrank significantly, (2)
questions.solution:
The error is in part (2) of the sentence. The helping verb "had" should be followed by the past participle (third form of verb) "shrunk", and not the simple past tense [second form] verb "shrank" since helping verbs "has", "have", and "had" are followed by past participles only.

The corrected sentence should read: "After I accidentally washed my favourite wool sweater in hot water, I was dismayed to see that it had shrunk significantly, becoming so small that it would now only fit a young child instead of a grown adult."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:

The ichthyologist identified the fish as a mort in its third year.

options.label: A
options.text: Upon the stag's demise, the hunter sounded a long, mournful mort on his horn.

options.label: B
options.text: The river was known for its healthy population of salmon and sea trout, including the occasional mort.

options.label: C
options.text: A mort is the name for a grilse, or young salmon, on its second return to the river.

options.label: D
options.text: The angler was pleased to have caught a sizable mort.

questions.correct_text: Upon the stag's demise, the hunter sounded a long, mournful mort on his horn.
questions.solution:
A homonym is a word that is spelled and pronounced the same as another word but has a different meaning.

In the original sentence, "mort" is a specific term for a young salmon in its third year.

In options (b), (c), and (d), "mort" is used with this exact same meaning, referring to the fish.

In option (a), "mort" refers to a specific note sounded on a hunting horn to signal that the hunted animal (like a stag) has been killed. This is a completely different meaning, making it the correct homonym.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the correct use of article 'the.'

options.label: A
options.text: The happiness is a goal that many people pursue throughout their lives.

options.label: B
options.text: She wrote a thoughtful essay about the importance of the kindness.

options.label: C
options.text: The patience he showed while teaching the children was truly admirable.

options.label: D
options.text: In business, the confidence is often considered a key to success.

questions.correct_text: The patience he showed while teaching the children was truly admirable.
questions.solution:
The correct sentence is option c).

Rule for "the" with abstract nouns: Generally, abstract nouns (like happiness, kindness, patience, confidence) do not take the definite article "the" when they are used in a general sense.

However, "the" is used when the abstract noun is followed by a qualifying phrase that specifies or limits it.

a): "Happiness" is used in a general sense here, so "the" is not needed. It should be "Happiness is a goal..."

b): "Kindness" is used in a general sense. It should be "...the importance of kindness."

c): Here, "patience" is not general; it's specifically the patience that he showed while teaching the children. The qualifying phrase "he showed while teaching the children" makes "the" necessary and correct.

d): "Confidence" is used in a general sense. It should be "...confidence is often considered a key to success."

Note: Abstract Noun: It is the name given to ideas, qualities, and conditions - things that cannot be seen or touched and things which have no physical reality. Some examples are, truth, danger, happiness, time, friendship, etc. This type of noun has no plural form.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article, 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

The festival committee kept adding subcommittees for food, decor, and security, and the head warned that too many cooks spoil the broth.

options.label: B
options.text: Too many people involved can ruin the task

options.text: Only experts should be allowed to help

questions.solution:
The proverb "too many cooks spoil the broth" means that when too many people are involved in managing a task, it can lead to confusion and poor results. In the sentence, the head warned against adding too many subcommittees for the festival.

questions.solution: The passage states, "Employees face job insecurity, loss of morale, and psychological stress.. Institutional knowledge.. is frequently lost when skilled workers are laid off or reassigned." (Paragraph 2) This highlights disruption as a negative effect. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Corporate restructuring is often presented as a necessary reform aimed at improving efficiency, competitiveness, and long-term sustainability. Organisations restructure in response to market pressures, technological change, financial crises, or strategic realignment. However, while restructuring is promoted as a tool for progress, it frequently raises the question of whether it genuinely leads to reform or merely results in disruption. From a reformist perspective, restructuring can revitalise stagnant organisations. By redefining roles, streamlining processes, and eliminating redundancies, companies seek to reduce costs and improve productivity. Mergers, acquisitions, and organisational redesigns are intended to create leaner structures that respond more effectively to consumer demands and global competition. In theory, restructuring enables innovation by removing bureaucratic obstacles and encouraging flexibility in decision-making.

Yet, in practice, corporate restructuring often produces significant disruption. Employees face job insecurity, loss of morale, and psychological stress as long-established teams are dismantled. Institutional knowledge, which develops over years of experience, is frequently lost when skilled workers are laid off or reassigned. This undermines organisational memory and weakens internal cohesion. Instead of fostering creativity, repeated restructuring may generate fear, compliance, and disengagement among employees. Moreover, the promised gains of restructuring are not always realised. Short-term financial improvements may mask long-term instability. Overemphasis on cost-cutting can compromise service quality, customer relationships, and ethical standards. When restructuring is driven primarily by shareholder interests, it risks ignoring the human and social dimensions of organisations. Workers become expendable resources rather than stakeholders in collective growth. Corporate restructuring also reflects a broader cultural obsession with constant change. In rapidly evolving markets, companies often equate transformation with survival, leading to continuous cycles of reorganisation. However, excessive restructuring can create confusion, disrupt workflows, and prevent employees from adapting fully to any single system. Stability, which is essential for learning and innovation, becomes undervalued.

questions.question: The word "redundancies" as used in the passage most nearly means:
questions.solution: In the passage, "eliminating redundancies" refers to removing repetitive or unnecessary positions or processes to streamline the organisation. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the following sentence.

The supervisor said that he was reviewing the trainee's performance report during the current week as part of the routine evaluation process.

options.label: A
options.text: The supervisor said, "I am reviewing your performance report this week as part of the routine evaluation process."

options.label: B
options.text: The supervisor said, "He was reviewing your performance report that week as part of the routine evaluation process."

options.label: C
options.text: The supervisor said, "I was reviewing your performance report that week as part of the routine evaluation process."

options.label: D
options.text: The supervisor said, "I have reviewed your performance report this week as part of the routine evaluation process."

questions.correct_text: The supervisor said, "I am reviewing your performance report this week as part of the routine evaluation process."
questions.solution:
The sentence in Indirect Speech is in the Past Continuous tense: "was reviewing".

When converting from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, Past Continuous can be changed to Present Continuous when the action is ongoing or currently relevant.

For example:

He said that he was checking the documents.

Direct: "I am checking the documents."

Changes when converting:

The reporting verb remains "said".

The verb changes from "was reviewing" to "am reviewing".

Pronouns change appropriately ("he" → "I", "the trainee's" → "your").

The time reference changes from "that week" to "this week".

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: What is the main objective of NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), set up under the Department of Space?
questions.question_hi: न्यूस्पेस इंडिया लिमिटेड (NSIL) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है, जो अंतरिक्ष विभाग के तहत स्थापित किया गया है?

options.label: A
options.text: To regulate and give licenses to private space companies in India.
options.text_hi: भारत में निजी अंतरिक्ष कंपनियों को विनियमित करना और लाइसेंस देना।

options.label: B
options.text: To carry out scientific research and deep-space missions like Mangalyaan.
options.text_hi: वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान और मंगलयान जैसे गहरे अंतरिक्ष मिशनों को अंजाम देना।

options.label: C
options.text: To produce launch vehicles and sell ISRO's space technology to private companies.
options.text_hi: लॉन्च वाहनों का उत्पादन करना और ISRO की अंतरिक्ष तकनीक को निजी कंपनियों को बेचना।

options.label: D
options.text: To provide free satellite education and medical services in rural areas.
options.text_hi: ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में मुफ्त उपग्रह शिक्षा और चिकित्सा सेवाएं प्रदान करना।

questions.correct_text: To produce launch vehicles and sell ISRO's space technology to private companies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) acting as the commercial arm of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).

NSIL was established to:

Commercialize ISRO's technologies

Manufacture and market launch vehicles

Enable private sector participation in space activities

Regulation and licensing of private space activities is handled by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center (IN-SPACe).

Further Insights

NSIL was incorporated in 2019 under the Companies Act.

It enables industry to build PSLV and other launch vehicles.

IN-SPACe acts as the regulatory body for private space firms.

India's space reforms in 2020 opened the sector to private players.

questions.question: In India, the President appoints judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts based on the recommendation of which body?
questions.question_hi: भारत में, राष्ट्रपति किस निकाय की सिफारिश के आधार पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय और उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति करते हैं?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Collegium System.

Under current practice, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the President based on recommendations made by the Collegium, which consists of the Chief Justice of India and senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.

This system evolved through Supreme Court judgments (Second and Third Judges Cases).

Further Insights

The Collegium system is not mentioned in the Constitution.

It evolved through the Second Judges Case (1993).

The NJAC was declared unconstitutional in 2015.

The President formally appoints judges after Collegium recommendation.

Judicial independence is the main principle behind this system.

questions.question:
With reference to the Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme (TAPS), consider the following statements:

i) The scheme guarantees state employees a pension equal to 50% of their last drawn basic pay, with a mandatory employee contribution of 10%.

ii) In the event of a pensioner's death, the family pension is fixed at 100% of the final pension amount received by the deceased.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
तमिलनाडु आश्वस्त पेंशन योजना (TAPS) के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i) यह योजना राज्य कर्मचारियों को उनकी अंतिम प्राप्त मूल वेतन का 50% पेंशन की गारंटी देती है, जिसमें 10% कर्मचारी योगदान अनिवार्य है।

ii) पेंशनधारी की मृत्यु की स्थिति में, परिवार पेंशन मृतक द्वारा प्राप्त अंतिम पेंशन राशि का 100% निर्धारित की जाती है।

उपरोक्त दिए गए कौन से कथन सही हैं?

options.label: D
options.text_hi: न तो I और न ही ii

questions.solution:
Under the Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme (TAPS), eligible Tamil Nadu government employees are assured a pension equal to 50% of their last drawn basic pay.

Employees are required to contribute 10% of their basic salary toward the pension fund - the rest of the liability is borne by the state government.

Further Insights

TAPS blends features of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) and National Pension System (NPS).

The scheme includes Dearness Allowance (DA) revisions twice a year.

A gratuity benefit of up to ₹25 lakh is available under TAPS.

TAPS is mandatory for employees joining after January 1, 2026.

The government bears the remaining pension cost beyond employee contributions.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the Verma Committee set up by the Government of India in 1999?
questions.question_hi: 1999 में भारत सरकार द्वारा स्थापित वर्मा समिति का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?

options.label: A
options.text: To suggest how to implement a Uniform Civil Code across India.
options.text_hi: भारत में एक समान नागरिक संहिता लागू करने के लिए सुझाव देना।

options.label: B
options.text: To examine legal provisions for implementing Fundamental Duties of citizens.
options.text_hi: नागरिकों के मौलिक कर्तव्यों को लागू करने के लिए कानूनी प्रावधानों की जांच करना।

options.label: C
options.text: To recommend changes in the appointment of Election Commissioners.
options.text_hi: चुनाव आयुक्तों की नियुक्ति में बदलाव की सिफारिश करना।

options.label: D
options.text: To study the 1991 economic crisis and suggest fiscal reforms.
options.text_hi: 1991 के आर्थिक संकट का अध्ययन करना और वित्तीय सुधारों का सुझाव देना।

questions.correct_text: To examine legal provisions for implementing Fundamental Duties of citizens.
questions.solution:
The 1999 Verma Committee (headed by Justice J.S. Verma) was set up to examine how Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Constitution could be implemented effectively.

It identified existing laws that already supported the enforcement of Fundamental Duties and suggested measures to strengthen awareness and compliance.

Further Insights

Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976).

There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties.

They are non-justiciable but supported by various laws.

Justice J.S. Verma later headed the 2013 committee on criminal law reforms.

The first phase of the Khelo India Winter Games 2026, held in Leh, Ladakh, saw Haryana top the overall medal standings.

Haryana secured the highest number of medals with multiple golds across events including figure skating and ice sports.

Further Insights

Figure skating made its debut in the Khelo India Winter Games 2026.

Ice hockey remains a marquee winter event at the Games.

Ladakh and Maharashtra were among the next top performers.

The Games are part of India's push to expand winter sports infrastructure.

questions.question:
With reference to the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), consider the following statements:

i) SAFTA was operationalised in 2006 as a successor to the South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) with the long-term objective of moving toward deeper economic integration in South Asia.

ii) Intra-regional trade within the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) region is currently comparable to the levels of trade integration seen in ASEAN and the European Union.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
दक्षिण एशियाई मुक्त व्यापार क्षेत्र (SAFTA) के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i) SAFTA को 2006 में दक्षिण एशियाई प्रेफरेंशियल ट्रेडिंग अरेंजमेंट (SAPTA) का उत्तराधिकारी बनाकर लागू किया गया था, जिसका दीर्घकालिक उद्देश्य दक्षिण एशिया में गहरे आर्थिक एकीकरण की ओर बढ़ना है।

ii) दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संघ (SAARC) क्षेत्र के भीतर आंतरिक क्षेत्रीय व्यापार वर्तमान में ASEAN और यूरोपीय संघ में देखे गए व्यापार एकीकरण के स्तर के समान है।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

options.label: D
options.text_hi: न तो i और न ही ii

questions.solution:
Statement i is correct.

SAFTA came into force in 2006 and replaced SAPTA. Its broader vision was gradual economic integration in South Asia, potentially paving the way toward deeper cooperation like a customs union or economic union in the long run.

Statement ii is incorrect.

Intra-regional trade within SAARC remains very low, typically around 5% of total trade of member countries. This is nowhere close to ASEAN (around 25%) or the European Union (over 60%).

• SAFTA replaced SAPTA in 2006 - correct.

• But South Asian countries don't trade much with each other - very low compared to ASEAN or EU.

Further Insights

SAFTA became operational on 1 January 2006.

Sensitive lists under SAFTA limit tariff reductions.

India - Pakistan tensions have significantly affected SAARC cooperation.

Informal trade in South Asia is estimated to be much higher than formal trade.

ASEAN and the EU have deeper institutional and economic integration compared to SAARC.

questions.question: Which physiological process describes the bone's role in maintaining a constant concentration of Calcium and Phosphorus in the blood?
questions.question_hi: कौन सी शारीरिक प्रक्रिया हड्डी की रक्त में कैल्शियम और फॉस्फोरस की स्थिर सांद्रता बनाए रखने में भूमिका को दर्शाती है?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Homeostasis.

Bones help regulate the levels of calcium and phosphorus in the blood by storing and releasing these minerals as needed. This regulation ensures that their concentration remains stable in the bloodstream.

This process of maintaining internal balance is called homeostasis.

Ossification

Ossification refers to the process of bone formation, where soft cartilage turns into hard bone.

Osteogenesis

Osteogenesis also means bone formation and development.

Hematopoiesis

Hematopoiesis is the formation of blood cells in bone marrow.

Further Insights

Parathyroid hormone increases blood calcium levels.

Calcitonin lowers blood calcium levels.

99% of body calcium is stored in bones and teeth.

Bone remodeling is a continuous lifelong process.

Vitamin D helps in calcium absorption from the intestine.

questions.question: At which railway station did Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurate India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper Train?
questions.question_hi: प्रधान मंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने भारत की पहली वंदे भारत स्लीपर ट्रेन का उद्घाटन किस रेलवे स्टेशन पर किया?
