questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The reporter said, "Addressing poverty is the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants".

options.label: A
options.text: The reporter said that addressing poverty had been the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants.

options.label: B
options.text: The reporter said that addressing poverty is the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants.

options.label: C
options.text: The reporter told that addressing poverty was the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants.

options.label: D
options.text: The reporter told that addressing poverty has been the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants.

questions.correct_text: The reporter said that addressing poverty is the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants.
questions.solution:
The sentence of the direct speech is in the simple present tense. A general fact is given about the mothers and their infants' nutrition, so there will be no change in the tense. 'That' will be used in place of inverted commas.

'Said' cannot change to 'told' in the given case because it needs a direct object after it, which is missing.

The correct choice will be - "The reporter said that addressing poverty is the key to improving the health and nutritional status of mothers and their infants."

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said to his assistant, "Go and switch on the alarm quickly."

options.label: A
options.text: He asked his assistant went and switched on the alarm quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: He ordered his assistant go and to switch on the alarm quickly.

options.label: C
options.text: He requested his assistant go and switch on the alarm quickly.

options.label: D
options.text: He ordered his assistant to go and switch on the alarm quickly.

questions.correct_text: He ordered his assistant to go and switch on the alarm quickly.
questions.solution:
Imperative Sentences are used to demonstrate Request, Order, Command, etc.

Imperative Sentences begin with Principal verbs like Go, Make, etc

The reporting verbs like "said", "say", etc. in direct speech are changed into "begged", "beg", etc.

"To" is used before the Principal Verbs in the Indirect Speech.

For example:

John said to his assistant, "Bring me a glass of water." (Direct Speech)

John ordered his assistant to bring him a glass of water. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

 The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'ordered'.

 "To" is used before the Principal Verb 'go'

Therefore, the correct answer is: He ordered his assistant to go and switch on the alarm quickly.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the tone adopted by the author in the passage?
questions.solution: The author examines how colour coding influences urban memory and identity through explanation and interpretation rather than praise or criticism. This is evident in analytical statements such as "This shift reflects the formation of a collective urban memory" and "signals a broader transformation in urban identity." Therefore, the tone is analytical and interpretative, making (a) the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

Colour coding in the Delhi Metro has done more than simplify navigation; it has reshaped how commuters mentally map the city. Over time, the coloured lines have become cognitive anchors through which urban space is remembered, described, and negotiated. Instead of relying on traditional geographical markers such as neighbourhood names or road junctions, many commuters now "think in lines." Expressions like "take the Yellow Line" or "it's on the Blue Line route" function as shared shorthand, replacing detailed spatial directions with instantly recognisable visual cues. This shift reflects the formation of a collective urban memory built around the metro network. Repeated daily travel reinforces associations between colours, routes, and experiences, embedding them into routine thought. The Yellow Line, for instance, is often linked with historical and administrative zones, while the Blue Line evokes long-distance commuting across residential and commercial hubs. Over time, these associations move beyond practical travel needs and become part of the city's lived consciousness. Colour coding also reduces cognitive effort in a densely populated and constantly evolving metropolis. By organising complexity into a limited set of visual categories, the metro allows commuters to recall routes quickly and communicate directions efficiently. This shared visual language enables strangers to coordinate effortlessly, even when they lack detailed knowledge of each other's destinations. In this way, colour-coded lines act as social connectors as much as transport corridors. Moreover, the replacement of geographical directions with line-based references signals a broader transformation in urban identity. The metro does not merely pass through the city; it actively structures how the city is imagined. As lines extend and intersect, they redraw mental maps, gradually shifting the focus from neighbourhood-based identities to network-based thinking. Thus, Delhi's colour-coded metro lines illustrate how infrastructure can shape collective memory, influencing not only movement through urban space but also the very way a city is thought about and spoken of.

questions.question: The phrase "cognitive anchors" in the passage most nearly refers to:
questions.solution: The phrase appears in the line, "the coloured lines have become cognitive anchors through which urban space is remembered, described, and negotiated." Here, "cognitive anchors" clearly refers to mental reference points that help commuters remember and organise urban space. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution: The word "many" stands independently to refer to an unspecified number of people, as seen in "many commuters now 'think in lines.'" It does not point to a specific noun (demonstrative), introduce a clause (relative), or refer back to the subject (reflexive). Therefore, it functions as an indefinite pronoun, making option (a) the correct answer.

Over time, the coloured lines have become cognitive anchors through which urban space is remembered, described, and negotiated. Instead of relying on traditional geographical markers such as neighbourhood names or road junctions, many commuters now "think in lines." Expressions like "take the Yellow Line" or "it's on the Blue Line route" function as shared shorthand, replacing detailed spatial directions with instantly recognisable visual cues. This shift reflects the formation of a collective urban memory built around the metro network. Repeated daily travel reinforces associations between colours, routes, and experiences, embedding them into routine thought. The Yellow Line, for instance, is often linked with historical and administrative zones, while the Blue Line evokes long-distance commuting across residential and commercial hubs. Over time, these associations move beyond practical travel needs and become part of the city's lived consciousness. Colour coding also reduces cognitive effort in a densely populated and constantly evolving metropolis. By organising complexity into a limited set of visual categories, the metro allows commuters to recall routes quickly and communicate directions efficiently. This shared visual language enables strangers to coordinate effortlessly, even when they lack detailed knowledge of each other's destinations. In this way, colour-coded lines act as social connectors as much as transport corridors. Moreover, the replacement of geographical directions with line-based references signals a broader transformation in urban identity. The metro does not merely pass through the city; it actively structures how the city is imagined. As lines extend and intersect, they redraw mental maps, gradually shifting the focus from neighbourhood-based identities to network-based thinking. Thus, Delhi's colour-coded metro lines illustrate how infrastructure can shape collective memory, influencing not only movement through urban space but also the very way a city is thought about and spoken of.

questions.question: Select the sentence that does NOT have a spelling error.

options.label: A
options.text: The scientist explained the phenomina behind the experiment in great detail.

options.label: B
options.text: She was delighted to receive the acknowlegement letter from the organisation.

options.label: C
options.text: The restaurant is famous for its authentic Italian cuisine.

options.label: D
options.text: He was extremely disapointed with the lack of enthusiasm among the participants.

questions.correct_text: The restaurant is famous for its authentic Italian cuisine.
questions.solution:
(a) - The correct spelling is phenomena (plural form of phenomenon), not phenomina. It means "a fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause or explanation is in question".

(b) - The correct spelling is acknowledgement. It means "acceptance of the truth or existence of something".

(d) - The correct spelling is disappointed (with double "p"), not disapointed. It means "sad or displeased because someone or something has failed to fulfil one's hopes or expectations".

The sentence that does NOT have a spelling error is (c). Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Peasants in grain-short areas may well be at loggerheads with those in grain-surplus areas.
questions.solution:
Be at loggerheads: disagree very strongly.

It is in context to peasants from grain deficit areas who are in disagreement with peasants from grain surplus areas.

The rest of the meanings are contextually incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a) disagree very strongly.

questions.question: The figure of speech used in "The classroom was a zoo during recess" is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (d) Metaphor.

A metaphor is a figure of speech that directly compares two unlike things by stating that one is the other. Here, the classroom is described as a zoo, implying it was noisy and chaotic. This comparison enhances the imagery without using "like" or "as."

Alliteration (option a) involves the repetition of initial consonant sounds (e.g., "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers"), which is absent here.

Irony (option b) expresses a meaning opposite to what is stated, often for humor or emphasis, which does not apply to this literal comparison.

Oxymoron (option c) combines two contradictory terms (e.g., "bittersweet" or "deafening silence"), which is not present in this sentence.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate adverb:

Despite the noisy corridor, the librarian spoke ____ so the visitors would not be disturbed.
questions.solution:
The blank describes how the librarian spoke, so it needs an adverb.

Option B (softly) is the adverb form of "soft," describing the manner of speaking.

Grammar rule used: Adverb vs adjective (adverb modifies a verb).

Example: "He speaks politely."

· Option A is an adjective; "spoke soft" is not correct in standard usage here.

· Option C is comparative and would require a comparison (e.g., "softer than before").

· Option D is a noun and cannot describe the verb "spoke."

Final correct sentence: Despite the noisy corridor, the librarian spoke softly so the visitors would not be disturbed.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb:

The manager asked the interns to ___ the summary before the meeting started.
questions.solution:
The meaning needed is "review/check quickly before a meeting."

Option C (go over) means to review something carefully or quickly before presenting it.

Vocabulary rule (phrasal verbs): Choose the verb that matches the intended action in context.

Example: "Let's go over the main points once more."

· Option A means "delay," which is the opposite of what is needed before a meeting.

· Option B means "take care of," which doesn't fit "summary" in this context.

· Option D means "meet by chance" or "encounter a problem," not "review."

Final correct sentence: The manager asked the interns to go over the summary before the meeting started.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with appropriate pronouns.

The manager was extremely impressed with the innovative marketing plan ________ the two new interns had developed together.
questions.solution:
The given sentence contains a main clause ("The manager was extremely impressed with the innovative marketing plan") and a relative clause describing the plan. The blank requires a pronoun to connect the clause to the noun "plan." Since "plan" is a thing and not a person, the correct pronoun must refer to an inanimate object.

The correct option is "which". "Which" is a relative pronoun used to introduce a clause that provides more information about a thing or idea previously mentioned. Here, it correctly refers to "the innovative marketing plan."

The other options are incorrect: "who" is used for people (as a subject); "whose" is used to show possession; "whom" is used for people (as an object).

Thus, the correct sentence is: "The manager was extremely impressed with the innovative marketing plan which the two new interns had developed together."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

questions.solution:

Rooster: an adult male chicken.

Occurrence: the fact of something existing, or how much of it exists.

Alex had a ___ twinkle in his eyes that toyed with the smile on his lips.
questions.solution:
Option (b) has the correctly spelt word. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

'Mischievous' means causing mischief or trouble.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He explained that he had been working on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet.

options.label: A
options.text: "I have been working on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet."

options.label: B
options.text: "I am working on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet."

options.label: C
options.text: "I worked on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet."

options.label: D
options.text: "I work on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet."

questions.correct_text: "I have been working on a complex research project about climate change for the past five years without any significant breakthroughs yet."
questions.solution:
The task involves converting a sentence from indirect (reported) speech to direct speech.

Key Rules for Reported Speech (Direct Speech)

When converting indirect speech to direct speech:

Change pronouns: Third-person pronouns (he) shift back to first-person ("I") based on the original speaker's perspective.

No time/place adjustments needed: Phrases like "for the past five years" remain unchanged as they are relative.

Forward shift tenses: Past perfect continuous ("had been working") shifts to present perfect continuous ("have been working") because the reporting verb ("explained") is in past, but direct restores original ongoing past-to-present tense.

No changes needed for: Adjectives like "complex" or the negative "without any significant breakthroughs yet."

Structure: Remove "that," add quotation marks and punctuation to form direct statement.

Option (a) correctly applies all rules: Pronouns shift ("he" → "I"), and "had been working" → "have been working" (forward shift). The sentence preserves the original meaning without errors.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Momentous
questions.solution: 'Momentous' means 'Of great importance or significance, especially in having a bearing on future events'. Options a) and c) can be rejected as they are unrelated to the word. 'Unsubstantial' means 'Having little or no solidity, reality, or factual basis'. Hence, option d) can also be rejected as it is the exact opposite. 'Construe' means 'Interpret (a word or action) in a particular way'. 'Eloquent' means 'Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing'. Hence, option b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: What is the closest meaning of the word "integral" as used in the sentence, "Emotional and social competencies are increasingly recognized as integral to a student's overall development"?
questions.solution:
The word "integral" implies something that is essential or indispensable. The sentence suggests that emotional and social competencies are a necessary part of development.

Option (a) is incorrect, as it contradicts the emphasis on importance.

Option (c) is incorrect, as "integral" does not imply temporality.

Option (d) is incorrect, as the passage highlights a close connection, not separation.

Hence, option (b) is correct.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the contemporary education landscape, the concept of learning has expanded beyond textbooks and examination scores. Emotional and social competencies are increasingly recognized as integral to a student's overall development. Schools are no longer viewed solely as spaces for academic instruction; they are also environments where attitudes, values, and interpersonal skills are shaped. This shift has emerged from the realization that intellectual ability alone does not guarantee personal fulfillment or professional success. Students who lack emotional awareness or social adaptability may struggle to apply their knowledge effectively, despite strong academic performance.

Multiple influences contribute to the development of emotional and social skills in students. Classroom dynamics, teacher-student relationships, and peer interactions play a significant role in shaping behaviour and self-perception. Competitive academic settings can sometimes heighten stress, discouraging collaboration and empathy. Additionally, excessive emphasis on grades may limit opportunities for students to engage in reflective thinking or cooperative problem-solving. When emotional needs are overlooked, students may experience disengagement, reduced motivation, or difficulty managing pressure, which can indirectly affect academic outcomes.

Recognizing these challenges, educational institutions are gradually adopting more holistic approaches to student development. Programs focusing on emotional literacy, teamwork, and communication are being integrated into curricula. Teachers are encouraged to create inclusive classrooms that value discussion and mutual respect. Parental involvement also supports this process by reinforcing emotional learning beyond school settings. By balancing academic rigor with emotional and social development, education systems aim to prepare students not only for examinations but also for complex real-world situations that demand resilience, adaptability, and ethical judgment.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the dominant tense used in the first paragraph?
questions.solution:
The first paragraph uses verbs such as "are recognized," "are shaped," and statements like "Schools are no longer viewed," which collectively emphasize general facts and ongoing realities.

While "has expanded" appears, the paragraph mainly relies on the Simple Present to state general truths about education and learning.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

Option (c) is not discussed in the passage.

Option (d) is unrelated to emotional neglect in the context provided.

options.text: We bought these steel bars from the famous store in town.

options.label: D

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Neither of them were competent/ to do that type of business and/ they made an expensive mistake.

options.label: C
options.text: to do that type of business and

questions.solution:
'Neither' denotes 'none of two things/persons' so it is followed by a singular form of verb. So, 'were' will be replaced with 'was' to make a grammatically right sentence.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Shamita finally revealed truth about what happened that night.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'revealed truth'. The error lies in the lack of an article before the noun "truth." When we refer to a specific, singular noun like "truth," we use the definite article to specify it. The context refers to a specific truth that Shamita revealed. The correct article to use in this context is the definite article "the." Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Shamita finally revealed the truth about what happened that night.

NOTE:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

She (decide to invest) her savings in a diverse portfolio of stocks and bonds, aiming for long-term growth and financial stability.
questions.solution:
In this sentence, the plural verb "decide" is incorrect to use with the singular subject 'she'. Option (d) is the correct choice. It uses the past tense "decided," accurately reflecting the action of deciding in the past to invest in a diverse portfolio.

The rest of the options are grammatically incorrect.

Option (a) is incorrect as 'was' needs to be followed by either the third form of the verb or the -ing form of the verb, but 'decide' is a base verb.

Options (b) and (c) - 'Are' and 'have' (plural verbs) cannot be used for the singular subject 'she'.

The corrected sentence: She decided to invest her savings in a diverse portfolio of stocks and bonds, aiming for long-term growth and financial stability.

questions.question:
Some sentences are given below. While the first and the last sentences (I and II) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

I. Hey, how was your weekend?

A. Do you have any plans for the upcoming holidays?

B. Sometimes a laid-back weekend is exactly what we need.

C. It was great! I went hiking with some friends.

D. That sounds amazing! I just stayed home and watched Netflix.

II. Not yet, but I'm thinking of taking a short trip to the beach. How about you?
questions.solution: The response in statement C matches statement I, as it talks about how the weekend was spent doing a fun activity, which was going hiking with friends. D should follow C as it directly responds to the other person's mention of spending the weekend. The response given in B could be relevant, as it acknowledges the mention of the weekend and reflects on the idea of having a relaxed weekend. A should be placed at the last because it is the question of the answer given in statement II. So, rearranging sentences in the order of CDBA forms a coherent paragraph. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Some sentences are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the four sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

S1. Vertical farming is an innovative agricultural practice of growing crops in vertically stacked layers, often integrated into buildings or shipping containers.

A. This method significantly reduces the need for land and allows for crop production in urban areas, closer to the consumers who need fresh produce.

B. By using soilless farming techniques such as hydroponics or aeroponics, this approach allows for precise control over environmental conditions like light, temperature, and nutrients.

C. Moreover, by recycling water within a closed-loop system, these farms can use up to 95% less water than traditional field farming methods.

D. Such controlled-environment agriculture ensures year-round production, independent of weather conditions, and eliminates the need for pesticides.

S6. As the world's population becomes increasingly urbanized, this technology offers a promising solution to enhance food security and reduce the environmental impact of agriculture.
questions.solution:
S1 defines vertical farming. The paragraph should explain its methods and benefits. Sentence B is the best starting point as it describes the core technology of "this approach" (hydroponics/aeroponics) and the control it provides. Sentence D explains the direct benefits of "Such controlled-environment agriculture" mentioned in B, such as year-round production and no need for pesticides. Sentence A explains a different, major benefit of "This method": the reduction in land use and its suitability for urban areas. Sentence C adds "Moreover," presenting another key advantage related to water conservation. The sequence BDAC logically flows from the core technology, to its immediate benefits, and then to broader benefits concerning land and water.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order with the first part being fixed. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

The SEND system is

B. With additional needs

C. The system that supports

D. Throughout their education

E. Children and young people
questions.solution:
The correct order to form a meaningful sentence is CEBD. The fixed part introduces the main topic of the sentence- The SEND system. Part C follows the fixed part as it continues the introduction by specifying what the SEND system does (it supports someone/something). Part E then identifies who the SEND system supports (children and young people). Accordingly, CE forms a logical pair. Part B further qualifies the children and young people being supported. It conveys that the system supports those children and young people who have some additional needs. Part D then indicates the scope or duration of the support. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The SEND system is the system that supports children and young people with additional needs throughout their education.

questions.question: Which idiom means to work extremely hard?

options.label: B
options.text: Let the cat out of the bag

questions.solution:
Burn the midnight oil - Correct. It means to work late into the night or work very hard, especially studying or doing a task.

Let the cat out of the bag - Means to reveal a secret unintentionally.

Spill the beans - Means to disclose secret information.

Hit the sack - Means to go to bed or sleep.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They baked the cake and sent it to the orphanage.

options.label: A
options.text: The cake was sent to the orphanage by them.

options.label: B
options.text: The cake had been baked and sent to the orphanage by them.

options.label: C
options.text: The cake was baked and sent to the orphanage by them.

options.label: D
options.text: They had baked the cake and it was sent to the orphanage by them.

questions.correct_text: The cake was baked and sent to the orphanage by them.
questions.solution:
The sentence is in past simple tense.

The sentence structure of the given active voice is: Subject [they] + Verb [baked] + Object [cake]

The subject and object of the active voice should be changed into the object and subject of the passive voice respectively.

While doing conversion, the conveyed meaning and the tense of the sentence should not be changed.

So, the passive voice formation of the sentence is: ‘Subject [cake] + was/were + Past participle verb [baked] + by + Object [them] ’.

Since the subject of the passive voice 'cake' is a singular noun, we should use 'was' as the helping verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The cake was baked and sent to the orphanage by them.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which description most accurately reflects the author's tonal stance in the passage?
questions.solution:
Solution:

The author critically examines the limitations of language while also reflecting on its social and emotional implications. This balanced critique is evident in lines such as "language often operates as a barrier, limiting understanding rather than enabling it" and the concluding emphasis on sensitivity and context. Therefore, the tone is best described as critical yet reflective. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions :Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

Language is commonly understood as a means of communication, a tool that allows individuals to share ideas, emotions, and knowledge. However, beyond this functional role, language often operates as a barrier, limiting understanding rather than enabling it. Far from being a transparent medium, language shapes perception, creates divisions, and determines whose voices are recognised within a society. One major way in which language becomes a barrier is through difference. Variations in language, dialect, and accent frequently lead to exclusion and misunderstanding. When people do not share a common linguistic code, communication becomes fragmented, and assumptions replace clarity. Even within the same language, social and regional variations can cause speakers to be judged, misunderstood, or dismissed, turning language into a marker of belonging and exclusion. Language also functions as a barrier through complexity and control. Technical, legal, or bureaucratic language often prioritises precision over accessibility, making essential information difficult for ordinary people to grasp. Such specialised forms of expression create a divide between those who possess linguistic authority and those who do not. As a result, language reinforces power structures by privileging certain groups while silencing others. Moreover, language struggles to capture the full range of human experience. Emotions such as grief, fear, or moral conflict often resist precise articulation, leaving speakers unable to express what they truly feel. In these moments, language fails not because of a lack of words, but because experience exceeds verbal boundaries. This gap between feeling and expression can lead to frustration, isolation, and misunderstanding. Finally, language can distort meaning through ambiguity and interpretation. Words are shaped by context, intention, and perspective, and meaning often changes as messages pass from one speaker to another. Thus, even sincere attempts at communication may result in confusion rather than understanding. In recognising language as a barrier, it becomes clear that communication requires more than words alone. Sensitivity, context, and active listening are essential to overcome the limitations imposed by language itself.

questions.question: According to the passage, why does specialised language create social division?

options.label: A
options.text: It removes emotional nuance from speech

options.label: B
options.text: It restricts access to essential information

options.label: C
options.text: It prevents cultural exchange across groups

questions.correct_text: It restricts access to essential information
questions.solution:
Solution:

The passage states that "Technical, legal, or bureaucratic language often prioritises precision over accessibility, making essential information difficult for ordinary people to grasp." This directly explains how specialised language creates division by limiting access. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.passage:
Directions :Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

Language is commonly understood as a means of communication, a tool that allows individuals to share ideas, emotions, and knowledge. However, beyond this functional role, language often operates as a barrier, limiting understanding rather than enabling it. Far from being a transparent medium, language shapes perception, creates divisions, and determines whose voices are recognised within a society. One major way in which language becomes a barrier is through difference. Variations in language, dialect, and accent frequently lead to exclusion and misunderstanding. When people do not share a common linguistic code, communication becomes fragmented, and assumptions replace clarity. Even within the same language, social and regional variations can cause speakers to be judged, misunderstood, or dismissed, turning language into a marker of belonging and exclusion. Language also functions as a barrier through complexity and control. Technical, legal, or bureaucratic language often prioritises precision over accessibility, making essential information difficult for ordinary people to grasp. Such specialised forms of expression create a divide between those who possess linguistic authority and those who do not. As a result, language reinforces power structures by privileging certain groups while silencing others. Moreover, language struggles to capture the full range of human experience. Emotions such as grief, fear, or moral conflict often resist precise articulation, leaving speakers unable to express what they truly feel. In these moments, language fails not because of a lack of words, but because experience exceeds verbal boundaries. This gap between feeling and expression can lead to frustration, isolation, and misunderstanding. Finally, language can distort meaning through ambiguity and interpretation. Words are shaped by context, intention, and perspective, and meaning often changes as messages pass from one speaker to another. Thus, even sincere attempts at communication may result in confusion rather than understanding. In recognising language as a barrier, it becomes clear that communication requires more than words alone. Sensitivity, context, and active listening are essential to overcome the limitations imposed by language itself.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to a active voice structure.

All the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony will have been made by the event planners by next weekend.

options.label: A
options.text: The event planners will be making all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.

options.label: B
options.text: The event planners will have to make all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.

options.label: C
options.text: The event planners will make all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.

options.label: D
options.text: The event planners will have made all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.

questions.correct_text: The event planners will have made all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['been' in the given sentence] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

For example:

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): The event planners will have made all the necessary arrangements for the grand wedding ceremony by next weekend.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that changes in the Fourth Schedule (Rajya Sabha seat allocation) due to reorganisation of states do not require a constitutional amendment under Article 368?

questions.solution:
Article 4 clearly states that:

Laws made under Article 2 and Article 3 (creation, merger, or reorganisation of states)

May include changes in the First and Fourth Schedules

And such changes do not count as constitutional amendments under Article 368

Article 2

Deals with admission or establishment of new states,

Article 3

Deals with formation or reorganisation of states

Article 5

Relates to citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

Further Insights

• Fourth Schedule deals with Rajya Sabha seat allocation

• Article 3 requires only a simple majority in Parliament

• Article 368 is used for formal constitutional amendments

• This provision ensures administrative flexibility

• Used during creation of states like Telangana

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding biological processes in living organisms:

i) Metabolism refers exclusively to the breakdown of complex molecules to release energy for cellular activities.

ii) Excretion is the physiological process of eliminating undigested food remains and toxic metabolic by-products from the body.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
जीवित जीवों में जैविक प्रक्रियाओं के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i) चयापचय केवल जटिल अणुओं को तोड़कर कोशिकीय गतिविधियों के लिए ऊर्जा जारी करने को संदर्भित करता है।

ii) उत्सर्जन शरीर से अपचनीय भोजन के अवशेषों और विषैले चयापचयी उपोत्पादों को निकालने की शारीरिक प्रक्रिया है।

उपरोक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?

options.label: A
options.text: Both statements i and ii are correct
options.text_hi: दोनों कथन i और ii सही हैं

options.label: D
options.text: Neither statement i nor ii is correct
options.text_hi: न तो कथन i सही है और न ही ii सही है

questions.correct_text: Neither statement i nor ii is correct
questions.solution:
statement (i) is incorrect

Metabolism does not refer exclusively to breakdown processes. It includes:

Catabolism → breakdown of molecules (energy-releasing)

Anabolism → synthesis of complex molecules (energy-requiring)

Since the statement mentions only breakdown, it gives an incomplete and incorrect definition.

Statement (ii) is incorrect

Excretion involves removal of metabolic wastes (like urea, CO₂, excess salts), not undigested food.

Removal of undigested food = Egestion

Removal of metabolic waste = Excretion

By mixing both processes, the statement becomes conceptually wrong.

Further Insights

• Metabolism occurs in all living cells, even in unicellular organisms

• Anabolism is essential for growth and repair

• Catabolism provides energy (ATP) for life processes

• Excretion helps maintain internal chemical balance (homeostasis)

• Egestion and excretion are entirely different biological processes

questions.question: What is the prescribed water temperature range for a standard Olympic-size swimming pool to ensure athlete performance and safety, as per international competition standards?
questions.question_hi: अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिता मानकों के अनुसार, एथलीट के प्रदर्शन और सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने के लिए एक मानक ओलंपिक आकार के स्विमिंग पूल के लिए निर्धारित जल तापमान सीमा क्या है?
questions.solution:
According to international swimming regulations issued by World Aquatics (formerly FINA),

· The ideal competition pool temperature must be maintained between 25°C and 28°C.

This range:

· Prevents muscle stiffness (if water is too cold)

· Avoids overheating and fatigue (if water is too warm)

Further Insights

• Olympic-size pools are 50 metres long

• Water temperature is checked before and during events

• Air temperature is usually kept 1 - 2°C higher than water

• Warm water increases cardiovascular strain

• Temperature control is critical for fair competition

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the redemption of financial instruments:

i) Redeemable instruments carry a predetermined maturity date on which the issuing company is legally obligated to repay the principal amount to the holders.

ii) Irredeemable instruments, also known as perpetual securities, do not have a fixed repayment date and are generally settled only when the company undergoes liquidation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
वित्तीय उपकरणों की पुनर्भुगतान के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i) पुनर्भुगतान योग्य उपकरणों में एक पूर्वनिर्धारित परिपक्वता तिथि होती है जिस पर जारी करने वाली कंपनी धारकों को मूलधन राशि चुकाने के लिए कानूनी रूप से बाध्य होती है।

ii) अप्रत्याशित उपकरण, जिन्हें स्थायी प्रतिभूतियां भी कहा जाता है, में निश्चित पुनर्भुगतान तिथि नहीं होती है और आमतौर पर केवल तब निपटाए जाते हैं जब कंपनी परिसमापन प्रक्रिया से गुजरती है।

उपरोक्त दिए गए कौन से कथन सही हैं?

options.label: D
options.text_hi: न तो i और न ही ii

questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct

Redeemable instruments (like redeemable debentures or preference shares) have:

o A fixed maturity date

o A legal obligation on the issuer to repay the principal

Statement (ii) is correct

Irredeemable instruments are also called perpetual securities.

They:

o Have no fixed repayment date

o Are usually repaid only during liquidation or winding up

Further Insights

• Redeemable preference shares are common in companies

• Perpetual instruments reduce short-term repayment pressure

• Investors demand higher returns for irredeemable securities

• Redemption improves a company's capital structure

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding biodiversity conservation strategies:

i) In-situ conservation involves protecting a species within its natural habitat through the establishment of National Parks and Biosphere Reserves.

ii) Ex-situ conservation refers to the protection of endangered species in man-made environments outside their natural habitats, such as Zoological Parks and Seed Banks.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
जैव विविधता संरक्षण रणनीतियों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i) इन-सिटु संरक्षण में राष्ट्रीय उद्यानों और बायोस्फीयर रिजर्व्स की स्थापना के माध्यम से किसी प्रजाति को उसके प्राकृतिक आवास के भीतर संरक्षित करना शामिल है।

ii) एक्स-सिटु संरक्षण का तात्पर्य प्राकृतिक आवासों के बाहर मानव निर्मित पर्यावरणों में संकटग्रस्त प्रजातियों की सुरक्षा से है, जैसे कि चिड़ियाघर और बीज बैंक।

उपरोक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?

options.label: D
options.text_hi: न तो i और न ही ii

questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct

· In-situ conservation means on-site conservation.

· Species are protected where they naturally occur, along with their ecosystem.

· Examples include National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves.

Statement (ii) is correct

· Ex-situ conservation means off-site conservation.

· Species are protected outside their natural habitat in controlled conditions.

· Examples include zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, and gene banks.

Further Insights

• In-situ conservation maintains entire ecosystems

• Ex-situ conservation is a backup strategy

• Genetic diversity is better preserved through in-situ methods
