questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A strong verbal or written attack on someone or something.
questions.solution:
Polemic: A strong and often aggressive written or spoken attack on a particular opinion, belief, or person.

Eulogy: A speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, typically someone who has just died.

Critique: A detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

Exhortation: An address or communication emphatically urging someone to do something.

So, "a strong verbal or written attack" is a "polemic".

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The principal said to the volunteers, "Stand near the exit and do not let the queue spill onto the stairs."

options.label: A
options.text: The principal told the volunteers stand near the exit and do not let the queue spill onto the stairs.

options.label: B
options.text: The principal ordered the volunteers that they should stand near the exit and did not let the queue spill onto the stairs.

options.label: C
options.text: The principal ordered the volunteers to stand near the exit and not to let the queue spill onto the stairs.

options.label: D
options.text: The principal requested the volunteers to stand near the exit and not to let the queue spill onto the stairs.

questions.correct_text: The principal ordered the volunteers to stand near the exit and not to let the queue spill onto the stairs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option c.

Rule of Speech Conversion:

A command or order is usually reported with "ordered" or "commanded".

The verb changes to "to + base verb".

A negative command changes to "not to + base verb".

Example: The officer said, "Stay here and do not move." → The officer ordered them to stay there and not to move.

Here, the sentence is clearly an order.

So the best reporting verb is "ordered".

"Stand" changes to "to stand".

"do not let" changes to "not to let".

So Option c is correct.

Option a is wrong because told the volunteers stand is incorrect. It should be told the volunteers to stand.

Option b is wrong because did not let is not the correct form after reporting the command. It should be not to let.

Option d is wrong because requested changes the force of the sentence. The principal is giving an order, not making a polite request.

Final correct sentence: The principal ordered the volunteers to stand near the exit and not to let the queue spill onto the stairs.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The shortlisted candidate was offered an overseas assignment by the board after the final review.

options.label: A
options.text: The board had offered the shortlisted candidate an overseas assignment after the final review.

options.label: B
options.text: The board offered the shortlisted candidate an overseas assignment after the final review.

options.label: C
options.text: The board was offering the shortlisted candidate an overseas assignment after the final review.

options.label: D
options.text: The shortlisted candidate offered the board an overseas assignment after the final review.

questions.correct_text: The board offered the shortlisted candidate an overseas assignment after the final review.
questions.solution:
Option (b) is correct. The sentence is in SIMPLE PAST passive voice: "was offered." In active voice, it changes into simple past active: OFFERED. In a double-object structure, "the board" becomes the subject, and "the shortlisted candidate" remains the indirect object.

• Option (a): changes the tense to past perfect.

• Option (c): changes the tense to past continuous.

• Option (d): it reverses the subject and object incorrectly, resulting in a logically incorrect meaning.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the passage is split into four parts P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1.The internet has revolutionized access to information.

P.People can now learn new skills through online platforms.

Q.Earlier, obtaining information required visiting libraries.

R.Search engines make information available within seconds.

S.This has greatly enhanced learning opportunities.

6.Knowledge has therefore become more accessible than ever before.
questions.solution: The passage discusses how the internet has changed access to information. Q provides the earlier situation, when people had to visit libraries for information. P introduces one of the advantages of the internet, allowing people to learn new skills online. R further explains the convenience of modern technology by mentioning search engines providing information quickly. S summarizes the overall impact, stating that learning opportunities have increased. Thus, the correct sequence becomes: QPRS. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. Libraries have long been centres of learning and knowledge.

P. Today, many libraries also provide digital resources and online databases.

Q. Earlier, people visited libraries mainly to borrow printed books.

R. This has expanded access to information for a wider audience.

S. Students and researchers benefit greatly from these facilities.

6. As a result, libraries continue to remain valuable institutions.
questions.solution: The passage begins with a general statement about libraries. Q logically follows because it describes the earlier role of libraries in providing printed books. P then contrasts the past with the present by mentioning digital resources and databases. S explains that students and researchers benefit from these facilities. R then summarises the impact, stating that access to information has expanded. Thus, the correct sequence is QPSR. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1: Planting trees is one of the simplest yet most effective ways to combat climate change. P: Trees absorb carbon dioxide, release oxygen, and help regulate the global climate. Q: Neglecting reforestation and urban greening can accelerate global warming and environmental degradation. R: Forests also provide habitats for countless species, maintaining biodiversity. S: Urban trees can reduce pollution, lower temperatures, and improve the quality of life in cities. 6: Therefore, tree planting initiatives are essential for environmental balance and human well-being.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: a) PRSQ.

Opening Statement (1): Introduces tree planting as a method to fight climate change.

Sentence P: Explains the environmental benefits of trees.

Sentence R: Expands to ecological importance, such as biodiversity and habitats.

Sentence S: Focuses on urban benefits, linking physical environment improvements to human life.

Sentence Q: Highlights the consequences of ignoring tree planting, reinforcing P-R-S.

Thus, the logical sequence is PRSQ.

questions.solution:

Astute: Having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage; sagacious.

The other options - Pacific (peaceful), Benevolent (kind), and Timid (lacking courage) are antonyms or unrelated in meaning.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The homophone for the word "hole" is _______.
questions.solution:
A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and often a different spelling.

Hole (an opening or cavity) and whole (entire or complete) are pronounced the same way but have different meanings, making them homophones.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Heal - to recover from an injury.

Hale - strong and healthy.

Hope - to wish for something positive.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The lecturer spoke so quietly that he was scarcely _______ at the back of the hall.
questions.solution:
The sentence conveys that the lecturer spoke very quietly, so it is obvious that his voice might not be able to reach the back of the hall. Thus, 'audible (able to be heard)' is the correct choice for the blank. Since an adjective would fit in the blank to describe the way he spoke, the adverb 'necessarily' is eliminated. The rest of the options do not fit well in the given context.

'Credible' means able to be believed; convincing.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The old woman said to the young couple, "May you both live a long and happy life together filled with joy."

options.label: A
options.text: The old woman wished that the young couple should live a long and happy life together filled with joy.

options.label: B
options.text: The old woman told the young couple that they should live a long and happy life together filled with joy.

options.label: C
options.text: The old woman prayed for the young couple that they might live a long and happy life together filled with joy.

options.label: D
options.text: The old woman hoped the young couple to live a long and happy life together filled with joy.

questions.correct_text: The old woman prayed for the young couple that they might live a long and happy life together filled with joy.
questions.solution:
Optative Sentences are usually prayers or wishes. In these kinds of sentences, "said" in the Direct Speech is changed into "prayed", "wished", etc. "That" is used in place of Inverted Commas. The sentence is changed into its Assertive form i.e., "Subject + might/may + V1 + Object".

For example:

The father said to his son, "May God bless you!" (Direct Speech)

The father wished his son that God might bless him. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"said to" is changed to "prayed for" or "wished". In this context of a blessing, "prayed for" is very suitable.

"May you" is changed to "that they might".

The sentence becomes assertive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "The old woman prayed for the young couple that they might live a long and happy life together filled with joy."

Hence, option (c) is correct.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

My grandmother carefully handed me the antique silver tongs that belonged to her great-grandmother.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: The antique silver tongs that belonged to her great-grandmother were carefully handed to me by my grandmother.

options.label: D
options.text: The antique silver tongs belonging to her great-grandmother were being handed carefully to me by my grandmother.

questions.correct_text: The antique silver tongs that belonged to her great-grandmother were carefully handed to me by my grandmother.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The preposition "by" and the helping verb "were" are to be added.

Certain nouns exist in Plural form only. The verbs used with them are also used in plural form when converting them into Passive voice. "Tongs" is a plural noun, so it takes a plural verb ('were').

The active voice sentence is in the Past Indefinite tense.

For example:

He gave me trousers. (Active)

Trousers were given to me by him. (Passive)

The options except (c) use incorrect verb agreement or tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The antique silver tongs that belonged to her great-grandmother were carefully handed to me by my grandmother.

questions.question:

We are looking for a person who provides expert advice professionally for our crisis.
questions.solution:
Rescuer- a person who saves someone from a dangerous or difficult situation.

Among the given options, the word that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined phrase is option (b), 'consultant'.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. Select the correct direct speech option.

The invigilator ordered the candidates not to write anything until the second answer sheet was distributed.

options.label: A
options.text: The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not wrote anything until the second answer sheet is distributed."

options.label: B
options.text: The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not write anything until the second answer sheet is distributed."

options.label: C
options.text: The invigilator said to the candidates, "Did not write anything until the second answer sheet was distributed."

options.label: D
options.text: The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not write anything until the second answer sheet was distributed."

questions.correct_text: The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not write anything until the second answer sheet is distributed."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option b.

Rule of Speech Conversion for Orders:

An order in indirect speech becomes an imperative sentence in direct speech.

"Ordered someone not to..." changes into "said to someone, 'Do not...'"

After "do not", the base form of the verb is used.

Example:

Indirect: The officer ordered the guard not to open the gate.

Direct: The officer said to the guard, "Do not open the gate."

Here, the invigilator is giving a clear command.

So "not to write" becomes "Do not write".

"Was distributed" changes back to "is distributed" because the original instruction is being restored.

So the correct direct speech is:

The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not write anything until the second answer sheet is distributed."

• Option a is wrong because "Do not wrote" is grammatically incorrect. After "do not", we use the base verb "write".

• Option c is wrong because "Did not write" gives a past statement, not a command.

• Option d is wrong because "was distributed" still keeps the reported form.

Final correct sentence:

The invigilator said to the candidates, "Do not write anything until the second answer sheet is distributed."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Jump the shark

options.label: A
options.text: To take a dangerous and life-threatening risk

options.label: B
options.text: The point at which something, once popular, declines into absurdity

options.label: C
options.text: To achieve sudden and unexpected success

options.label: D
options.text: To switch one's loyalty or allegiance at a critical time

questions.correct_text: The point at which something, once popular, declines into absurdity
questions.solution:
This is a modern idiom used to describe the moment when a creative work (like a long-running television show) begins a decline in quality, often marked by a particularly ridiculous plot twist intended to maintain viewers' interest.

For example: "Many fans felt the series jumped the shark when the main characters were abducted by aliens."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question:

An albatross around one's neck

options.label: C
options.text: A persistent and burdensome problem or source of guilt

options.label: D
options.text: To be protected by a powerful entity

questions.correct_text: A persistent and burdensome problem or source of guilt
questions.solution:
This idiom refers to a heavy burden of guilt or a persistent problem that is a constant reminder of a past mistake.

For example: "The massive debt from his failed business became an albatross around his neck for years."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Jennifer said, "I was calculating my expenses last night with the help of a calculator on the desk."

options.label: A
options.text: Jennifer said that she was calculating her expenses the previous night with the help of a calculator on the desk.

options.label: B
options.text: Jennifer said that she had been calculating her expenses the previous night with the help of a calculator on the desk.

options.label: C
options.text: Jennifer said that she has been calculating her expenses the previous night with the help of a calculator on the desk.

options.label: D
options.text: Jennifer said that she had been calculating her expenses last night with the help of a calculator on the desk.

questions.correct_text: Jennifer said that she had been calculating her expenses the previous night with the help of a calculator on the desk.
questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were+ first form of verb + ing + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + first form of verb + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I was watching television last night" (Direct Speech)

He said that he had been watching television the previous night. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:
Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
saidsaid that
Ishe
washad been
myher
last nightthe previous night

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) Jennifer said that she had been calculating her expenses the previous night with the help of a calculator on the desk.

questions.question: What is the main argument of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Public discussions about feminism have increased in modern society

options.label: B
options.text: Some individuals adopt feminist language without genuine commitment

options.label: C
options.text: Patriarchal attitudes remain visible in many social environments

options.label: D
options.text: Feminist ideas encourage greater awareness about gender equality

questions.correct_text: Some individuals adopt feminist language without genuine commitment
questions.solution: The passage focuses on the contrast between genuine allies of feminism and individuals who adopt feminist language merely as a social identity. Paragraph 2 explains that such individuals may publicly claim progressive views while privately holding patriarchal assumptions. Paragraph 3 further highlights that this behaviour erodes trust and weakens authentic discussions about gender justice. Therefore, the central argument is that some people use feminist language without sincere commitment to its principles. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

In contemporary discussions on gender equality, the language of feminism has become increasingly common. Many men openly identify themselves as supporters of women's rights and claim to stand in solidarity with feminist ideals. While genuine allies certainly exist, there is also a category of individuals who adopt the label of feminism merely as a social identity rather than a sincere commitment. Their support often appears persuasive on the surface, as they speak the vocabulary of equality and publicly criticise discrimination against women.

However, this performative alignment with feminism can sometimes conceal attitudes that remain deeply patriarchal. A man who openly expresses misogynistic views is usually easier to identify and confront because his position is explicit. In contrast, someone who claims to be progressive while privately perpetuating sexist assumptions may gain trust and social credibility. By presenting themselves as enlightened allies, such individuals often avoid scrutiny and criticism. This contradiction between words and actions allows them to maintain influence in spaces that are meant to promote equality.

The greater danger of such behaviour lies in the erosion of trust it creates. When feminist language is used merely as a tool for personal reputation or social approval, it weakens the authenticity of discussions about gender justice. Women and genuine allies may become sceptical of declarations of support, which ultimately harms collective efforts toward meaningful change. True allyship therefore demands consistency between public claims and private conduct, as well as a willingness to challenge one's own privileges rather than simply adopting the language of progress.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can performative supporters of feminism be more difficult to identify?

options.label: A
options.text: They openly criticise discrimination against women in public

options.label: B
options.text: They frequently avoid participating in debates on equality

options.label: C
options.text: They publicly express progressive views but privately differ

options.label: D
options.text: They usually lack understanding of feminist social theory

questions.correct_text: They publicly express progressive views but privately differ
questions.solution: The explanation is given in Paragraph 2, which states: "someone who claims to be progressive while privately perpetuating sexist assumptions may gain trust and social credibility." Because such individuals present themselves as enlightened allies, they avoid scrutiny and criticism. Their public statements therefore differ from their private attitudes, making them harder to identify than openly misogynistic individuals. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.

options.label: A
options.text: Engaging in a deep and contemplative process,

options.label: B
options.text: considering various perspectives and potential outcomes

options.label: C
options.text: before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.

options.label: D
options.text: she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities,

questions.correct_text: she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities,
questions.solution:
The adverb 'as' cannot be used with 'name, elect, think, consider, call, appoint, make, choose'. So, 'think as' will be changed to 'think about (give thought to)' in the given sentence.

The correct sentence is- "Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think about the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.

She explained the complex theory (so clear that everyone understood) it immediately afterwards.
questions.solution:
The error in the bracketed segment "so clear that everyone understood" is the use of the adjective "clear" where an adverb "clearly" is needed. The word should modify the verb "explained," describing how she explained.

a) "so clear because everyone understood" - "Clear" is still an adjective.

b) "very clear that everyone understood" - "Clear" (adjective) is again used incorrectly here.

c) "so clearly that everyone understood" - This option correctly uses the adverb "clearly" to modify the verb "explained."

d) "so clear for everyone understood" - "Clear" is still an adjective.

The correct sentence is: She explained the complex theory so clearly that everyone understood it immediately afterwards.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is option c).

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that uses a homonym of the underlined word:

He had a light lunch today.

options.label: A
options.text: The lamp gave off a bright light in the room.

options.label: B
options.text: He prefers a light dinner before bed.

options.label: C
options.text: She carried a light suitcase for travel.

options.label: D
options.text: He enjoys a light breakfast in the morning.

questions.correct_text: The lamp gave off a bright light in the room.
questions.solution:
Homonyms are words that are spelled the same and sound the same but have different meanings.

In the original sentence, "light" is an adjective meaning "not heavy."

Options b), c), and d) also use "light" in the same sense of "not heavy," so the meaning is similar.

Option a) uses "light" as a noun meaning "brightness," which is completely unrelated to the original meaning. This makes it a homonym.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an oxymoron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is c) An open secret.

An oxymoron is a figure of speech that combines two words with contradictory or opposite meanings. A "secret" is something kept from the knowledge of others. Therefore, an "open secret" is a contradiction, describing a piece of information that is supposed to be secret but is actually widely known.

The other options are not oxymorons because the words do not contradict each other. A night can be dark, a choice can be difficult, and a stop can be sudden.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with the correct collocation for the word 'risk'.

options.label: A
options.text: He was not afraid to make a risk.

options.label: B
options.text: He was not afraid to do a risk.

options.label: C
options.text: He was not afraid to take a risk.

options.label: D
options.text: He was not afraid to have a risk.

questions.correct_text: He was not afraid to take a risk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is c) He was not afraid to take a risk.

This is a very strong, standard, and common collocation in English. The phrase "to take a risk" is the classic phrase used to mean exposing oneself to danger or a chance of loss.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Fast Track Immigration-Trusted Traveller Program' (FTI-TTP) inaugurated by the union Home minister?
questions.question_hi: संघ गृह मंत्री द्वारा उद्घाटित 'फास्ट ट्रैक इमिग्रेशन-ट्रस्टेड ट्रैवलर प्रोग्राम' (FTI-TTP) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?

options.label: A
options.text: To provide subsidized international air tickets to Indian students studying abroad
options.text_hi: विदेश में पढ़ रहे भारतीय छात्रों को सब्सिडी वाले अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई टिकट प्रदान करना

options.label: B
options.text: To offer faster, smoother, and more secure immigration clearance through biometric verification
options.text_hi: बायोमेट्रिक सत्यापन के माध्यम से तेज़, सुगम और अधिक सुरक्षित आव्रजन मंजूरी प्रदान करना

options.label: C
options.text: To completely eliminate the requirement of a Visa for Indian nationals traveling to G20 countries
options.text_hi: G20 देशों की यात्रा करने वाले भारतीय नागरिकों के लिए वीज़ा की आवश्यकता को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना

options.label: D
options.text: To establish a centralized international passport authority under the Ministry of Home Affairs
options.text_hi: गृह मंत्रालय के तहत एक केंद्रीकृत अंतरराष्ट्रीय पासपोर्ट प्राधिकरण स्थापित करना

questions.correct_text: To offer faster, smoother, and more secure immigration clearance through biometric verification
questions.solution:
The Fast Track Immigration - Trusted Traveller Program (FTI-TTP) was launched by the Government of India to provide faster, smoother, and more secure immigration clearance for pre-verified travelers at international airports. The program uses automated e-gates and biometric verification so that registered travelers can clear immigration quickly without standing in long queues.

Further insights

• The program was launched in June 2024 at Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi.

• It is implemented by the Bureau of Immigration under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• The scheme is available for Indian passport holders and Overseas Citizen of India cardholders.

• Registered travelers can use special e-gates instead of traditional immigration counters.

• The program is being gradually expanded to several major international airports across India.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding 'Counter-Cyclical Fiscal Policy' is incorrect?
questions.question_hi: 'काउंटर-साइक्लिकल वित्तीय नीति' के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन गलत है?

options.label: A
options.text: During an economic recession, the government typically increases public spending.
options.text_hi: आर्थिक मंदी के दौरान, सरकार आमतौर पर सार्वजनिक खर्च बढ़ाती है।

options.label: B
options.text: During a period of economic boom, the government may increase tax rates to control inflation.
options.text_hi: आर्थिक उछाल के दौरान, सरकार मुद्रास्फीति को नियंत्रित करने के लिए कर दरें बढ़ा सकती है।

options.label: C
options.text: The primary goal of this policy is to follow the natural trend of the business cycle.
options.text_hi: इस नीति का मुख्य उद्देश्य व्यावसायिक चक्र की प्राकृतिक प्रवृत्ति का पालन करना है।

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing taxes during a downturn is a key tool used to boost aggregate demand.
options.text_hi: मंदी के दौरान करों में कटौती कुल मांग को बढ़ाने के लिए एक प्रमुख उपकरण है।

questions.correct_text: The primary goal of this policy is to follow the natural trend of the business cycle.
questions.solution:
Counter-cyclical fiscal policy refers to government actions that move in the opposite direction of the business cycle in order to stabilize the economy. During economic downturns, the government increases spending or reduces taxes to stimulate demand, and during economic booms it may reduce spending or increase taxes to control inflation.

Further insights

• Counter-cyclical fiscal policy is strongly associated with Keynesian economic theory.

• Fiscal stimulus packages are commonly used during recessions to revive economic growth.

• Automatic stabilizers such as unemployment benefits act as built-in counter-cyclical tools.

• High government spending during downturns may increase fiscal deficits in the short term.

• Central banks often complement fiscal policy with monetary policy to stabilize the economy.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

i. India topped the medal standings at the World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026 New Delhi leg with over 200 medals.

ii. Russia finished third in the medal tally, while Bosnia and Herzegovina secured second place.

iii. The event was held at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and featured athletes from eight countries.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

i. भारत ने वर्ल्ड पैराथलेटिक्स ग्रैंड प्रिक्स 2026 नई दिल्ली चरण में 200 से अधिक पदकों के साथ पदक तालिका में शीर्ष स्थान प्राप्त किया।

ii. रूस पदक तालिका में तीसरे स्थान पर रहा, जबकि बोस्निया और हर्जेगोविना ने दूसरा स्थान हासिल किया।

iii. यह आयोजन जवाहरलाल नेहरू स्टेडियम में हुआ और इसमें आठ देशों के एथलीटों ने भाग लिया।

उपरोक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is correct - India secured 208 medals and topped the standings.

Statement 2 is incorrect - Russia finished second, and Bosnia & Herzegovina was third.

Statement 3 is correct - The event took place at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and had 257 athletes from 8 countries.

Further insights

India finished on top of the medal standings at the World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026 New Delhi leg, securing 208 medals as the three-day competition concluded at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

The host nation won 75 gold, 69 silver and 64 bronze medals. Russia finished second with 35 medals, while Bosnia and Herzegovina placed third with three.

India's double Paralympic bronze medallist Preeti Pal won her second gold of the meet in the women's 200m T35-T37. India also secured podium sweeps in several events, including the men's shot put F57 where Shubham Juyal took gold with a 14.45-metre throw.

In the men's 200 meter T37-T44, Rakeshbhai Bhatt clocked 25.20 seconds to lead an all-Indian podium, while Manojkumar Sabapathi won gold in the men's 800 meter T53-T54.

The event featured 257 athletes from eight countries. Earlier in the meet, Paralympic champions Sumit Antil and Praveen Kumar also secured gold medals.

The New Delhi leg was the second stop of the 13th Grand Prix season, offering key international classification opportunities ahead of the 2026 World Para Athletics Championships and the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics.
